2026-09-01 · v4.113 — **§36 gains one decision and seven findings on cost of goods, and the finding comes first because it forces the decision: COST OF GOODS DOES NOT EXIST BEFORE CAPTURE STARTED AND CANNOT BE BACKFILLED.** `unit_cost_at_sale` capture landed in one commit — `6cc03f6c`, 2026-08-30 14:44:32 UTC, all six sale paths at once — so **every order line before it is NULL permanently**, and the column's own comment records why a backfill is refused: `retail_product_versions` keeps 25 versions per product, `activity_log` `cost_update` rows come only from PO receiving, the recipe rollup records nothing, and a backfill falling back to today's cost would produce a column that looks like a snapshot without being one. **The commit date is NOT the data cutoff** — deploy time is not commit time, `release.json` is stale, there is no deploy log in the repository, and two commits on the main line around 2026-09-01 concern the deploy hook shipping nothing silently; **the trustworthy cutoff is the earliest non-null row per channel, a query against production that HAS NOT BEEN RUN**, and any statement of the date must come from it rather than from the commit. **The consequence: the cutover starts 1 August and capture starts at the end of that month, so June and July have no cost data and never will, August has cost for its final days only, and gross profit does not exist for substantially the whole period the cutover covers.** **The decision that follows: a missing staircase step is SHOWN and marked NOT RECORDED, never hidden and never zero** — Summary renders both the cost of goods line and the gross profit line reading Not recorded, while revenue, operating expenses and net render normally from the data that exists. **Three alternatives are rejected with their reasons:** hiding the two lines leaves a reader opening July with no gross profit and no explanation, reasonably concluding the screen is broken; suppressing the middle step everywhere discards real data for September onward to keep the screen uniform; and **zero claims the goods were free — the same failure the cost column refuses at write time**, where every write site passes null rather than zero and `productUnitCostYuan` returns null rather than a stored zero, while a dash is already banned as a value. **Not recorded is the existing seventh state on §1.12 of `docs/tacet-desktop-patterns.md`**, added there from the pre-24-August Meituan orders — same problem, same treatment. **SIX WAYS THE COST READER WILL SILENTLY MISCOUNT are recorded as BINDING on its build**, each producing a plausible wrong number rather than an error: `unit_cost_at_sale` is per single unit, so the line's cost is `unit_cost_at_sale × qty × COALESCE(pack_units, 1)` and a Meituan or Eleme `qty` of 1 against a 6瓶 listing is six units off the shelf — **the revenue half takes no such multiplier**, `SUM(line_total)` being already correct, so a reader that treats the two halves alike is wrong on one of them; **itemised partial refunds** stamp `refunded_qty` and stop, with status, `qty` and `line_total` all unreduced and nothing subtracting it from any aggregate today, so a cost reader must sum `qty − COALESCE(refunded_qty, 0)`; **amount-only partial refunds are the hole that fix does NOT close** — nothing is written to the line at all, the refund lives on the order and in a `retail_refund_events` row, and **a reader working from order lines cannot see it at any level of sophistication**, so `qty − refunded_qty` is necessary and NOT sufficient and the itemised fix must not be read as complete; **`options_json` carries price deltas and no cost counterpart**, so cost is under-counted wherever a paid option costs the business something; **add-on lines go NULL, not zero, on a failed settlement-time re-derivation**; and **bundles are safe from double-counting** — one line per bundle, components never written as lines, cost through `bundleUnitCostYuan` rather than a raw `store_products.unit_cost` read that would record every bundle ever sold as free — **but the derivation is all-or-nothing, so a bundle NULL means one component was unpriced, not that the bundle was.** **TWO WAYS A NON-NULL COST IS STILL NOT WHAT IT APPEARS are recorded separately, being wrong numbers rather than missing ones:** `store_products.cost_incomplete` is three-state and **does not reach the line** — a product flagged incomplete still returns a positive number from `productUnitCostYuan`, snapshotted with no trace of the flag, and the flag lives on the mutable product row so it cannot be recovered for a past sale, leaving a knowingly understated line indistinguishable from a right one; and **`backfillGzMirrors` stamps TODAY's cost onto historic orders**, mirroring old gzgrocery orders into `retail_orders` at daemon startup with `gzUnitCost` read at mirror time, so **a present-day figure wears a historic date — precisely the failure the backfill refusal exists to prevent, occurring on one path anyway.** **gzgrocery must be ruled in or out of cost EXPLICITLY and no existing query answers it** — its rows are real fulfilled orders, included in order counts, trend and AOV and excluded from revenue sums, the exclusion is not even consistent across sites with the companion predicate declared separately four times, and no precedent exists because no existing query touches cost; recorded as an open item rather than decided. **The aggregation predicate and the order date are both inconsistent today, and the cost reader MUST NOT INHERIT BY PROXIMITY:** thirteen sites read `retail_order_items` in aggregate and none reads cost, there is no shared predicate, an allow-list is declared once and re-declared inline four more times, a deny-list is live at two sites and **is not equivalent** since it admits any status added later, and neither addresses partial refunds — while **four date conventions run simultaneously**, `COALESCE(paid_at, placed_at)` shifted `+8 hours` at five sites and dominant, `paid_at` alone unshifted which silently drops orders with a null `paid_at` and puts its day boundary in UTC, `placed_at` alone unshifted, and no date filter at all, so **an order placed 31 July at 22:00 Guangzhou and paid 1 August lands in August on one screen and July on another.** **A market or till sale has no cost of goods anywhere** — the market-stall POS and the kitchen app's manual sales entry both write `sales_entries`, which has `qty`, `unit_price` and `total` and no cost column at all; §36's counter-sales decision already covers it and is recorded here as **decided and unbuilt**, so until it is built a market sale contributes revenue with no cost, **which on the staircase reads as pure gross profit.** **Location attribution runs through the order header and is wrong in three known cases** — there is no location column on the order line and `retail_orders.store_id` is nullable with no default, so pre-column rows carry NULL and are silently dropped by any grouping; a **drop-ship** line never passes through a store yet inherits the order's `store_id`, so per-location cost would charge stock to a shop that never held it; a **split shipment** reports one location for lines that moved separately; and **`routing_reason = 'fallback_no_stock'`** is accurate about fulfilment and misleading about origin — all of which compounds the contribution dependency already standing on §36. **One open item is added to §36's *Explicitly NOT decided here*, and no existing standing line is edited or deleted.** Docs only; no code, no schema, no routes.

2026-09-01 · v4.112 — **§9 gains the market-stall decisions: a market is an ORDINARY LOCATION, and the stock closeout belongs to ENDING rather than to closing for the day.** A market stall requests stock through the existing restock flow, sells through POS and shows contribution like any other location — **one location per market, REUSED across visits, never one per occasion**, which would fragment contribution into single days that cannot be compared with each other and fill the locations list with dead entries; a three-day market is one location open for three days, restocking mid-run through the same flow. **Recorded explicitly as a CHANGE to current behaviour rather than a formalisation of it:** the kitchen POS deliberately moves no stock at a market and says so in its own header — markets sell from a stall replenished outside the system — so this is new behaviour on that path; but **the kitchen path is NOT being fixed and dies with the kitchen app**, and Tacet's till already decrements on paid, so the surviving path needs no change. **The return-path finding is recorded first, because a later session reading §9's existing move-out line will otherwise assume the mechanism is there to call:** `_applyRestockTransfer` is the only code in the repository that moves stock between locations and is hard-coded warehouse-to-destination; **`from_role`/`to_role` describe who asked whom, not which way goods travel** — a store-to-warehouse request moves stock FROM the warehouse TO the store; `transfer_in`/`transfer_out` sit in a schema comment with zero writers and zero readers; and the only route today is two unlinked `adjust` rows that no query can tell apart from a stocktake correction, usually not postable by one person because an operator may only edit their assigned location. **The decision is a CLOSEOUT: one action that asks what came back, moves it to the warehouse and ends the location.** A reverse transfer request was rejected as request-shaped — states to drive through are the wrong object to hand someone packing up at the end of a market day. **The ending/closing distinction is the substance of it:** a shop closes at night with stock on the shelf and opens with it there, so a nightly prompt is a daily question with the same answer and one people learn to dismiss unread, while a market ENDS and the stall is gone; **the closeout is therefore NOT attached to the Open/Closed toggle**, and in practice means markets, because markets are what end. **It ledgers both halves as ONE LINKED MOVEMENT**, which is what separates it from the manual workaround, with the warehouse as default destination and a choice on a permanent shop closure. **§36 gains a DEPENDENCY, not a decision, correcting an assumption carried through the location-dimension design: per-location contribution cannot be computed from current data.** Cost is recognised at purchase — `postRetailPOExpenses` posts on Ordered or Delivered, dated to the purchase order — nothing in the repository values inventory, and **`unit_cost_at_sale` is written on all six sale paths and read by nothing, as its own schema comment states.** Stock carried to a market and not sold is already expensed on the PO date whether it sells or not, so selling it changes nothing about cost. Nothing is reversed: the location dimension, the word CONTRIBUTION and *Finance reads `unit_cost_at_sale`* all stand — **what is recorded is that the reader is unbuilt work**, and that a contribution figure computed from the expense ledger alone would be wrong in a way that looks right. **Two open items are added to a new *Explicitly NOT decided here* on §9:** whether stock at a location closed for the day is ever checked — nothing verifies `sellableStockSql`'s moved-or-behind-a-shutter assumption and nothing reports the units, and a DEACTIVATED location is worse, its stock neither sold, counted nor reported — and whether a location needs an explicit "does not fulfil online" flag, since **an active location is automatically a fulfilment candidate** and a market stall is immediately eligible for a customer's online order; the `channel_status` workaround exists but is non-obvious, and the two switches an operator reaches for first would close POS too. **Three standing facts are recorded without deciding anything:** restock requests are auto-archived overnight, so a multi-day market's open request drops out of the Fulfill tab; **there is no Retired state on a location anywhere in schema or UI**, only `is_active`, so any spec naming one names something that does not exist; and `restock_items.product_id` points at the kitchen catalogue while the transfer writes `store_products` ids, so `_checkTransferIds` refuses the whole transfer and a market request carrying any post-fork product is refused outright rather than partially applied. **Two standing §9 lines are LEFT STANDING and superseded in place** on the usual convention — *market stalls again as new TEMPORARY locations*, narrowed to one per market, and *closing requires remaining stock to be moved to a named location*, narrowed to ending. Docs only; no code, no schema, no routes.

2026-09-01 · v4.111 — **§36 closes three of its four open items and flags one new cutover concern.** **`wechat_chat` and `pickup` were never unmapped and the open item asking what they are rested on a wrong premise:** they are staff-keyed order ORIGINS written by the New order form's "Order came from · 订单来源" dropdown alongside `wholesale` and `other`, not platform channels, and **the Sales-summary partition defines `direct` as a residual rather than an inclusion list**, so every channel value including ones not yet invented lands in exactly one bucket and no revenue can fall out — what they lack is a card of their own, not a mapping. **The collision that follows is a trap for any Finance query and is recorded as a rule: `pickup` is the same string in two columns with two unrelated meanings** — as `retail_orders.channel` it means the customer came to the shop to order, as `fulfillment_type` it means the customer collects later, a row can legitimately be both `channel='pickup'` and `fulfillment_type='delivery'`, and **a bare reference to "pickup" is ambiguous and must not appear in a spec.** **`wechat_chat` is not `wechat`** — the mini app writes its own orders, `wechat_chat` is a customer who messaged the shop and had the order hand-keyed, and `wechat` and `web` were deliberately removed from the manual list because staff-keyed rows claiming them were inflating self-serve revenue. **PO-derived expense rows STAY delete-and-reinsert projections, and the safety is enforced rather than incidental:** `routes/finance.js` refuses both edit and delete on any row carrying a `po_id`, so no human-authored value can accumulate on them, and no foreign key anywhere points at `expense_entries.id`, so regenerating ids breaks no stable reference. **The consequence is that `created_at` on a PO-derived row is not an audit timestamp** — it records the last re-post, not when the purchase happened, and must never be shown as a purchase date or used as evidence of when anything occurred; the purchase order's own date is the date to display, and Tacet's projection carries it. **A new cutover concern is FLAGGED, not resolved: `backfillOrderedExpenses()` is an uncontrolled writer to the money ledger** — it runs on every server start, finds any postable purchase order with zero expense rows and posts it, without anyone touching a purchase order, and it is the mechanism behind the expense table continuing to grow after export; **the kitchen expense table is not a closed archive while this runs**, and whether Tacet carries an equivalent is recorded as open. **How much of the 92 → 168 growth was the backfill is not merely unmeasured but UNDERIVABLE from `expense_entries`** — both posting paths call `postPOExpenses()`, no row records its caller, and `created_at` is rewritten on re-post — and the two sources that could answer are not established as retained: PO `status_change` rows sit in `activity_log`, purged past 90 days on every startup, and the backfill writes no `activity_log` row at all. **Income categories move server-side to the same `categories` table as expense, shared and hydrated from the server, and THE LIST SHIPS EMPTY.** Today they live in browser localStorage only and cannot be synced at all — `routes/lookups.js` does not accept `'income'` as a kind, so the endpoint would refuse — so every browser holds its own list and an edit on one machine is invisible on every other. **No defaults, and the reasoning is recorded so a later session is not tempted to seed it:** the current four are dine-in, takeaway, delivery and events, all fulfilment or channel facts the order record already carries, so an income category that restates the channel is a dropdown with one correct answer — **and a dropdown with a wrong option available is what produced the ¥152,309 Mini App mis-filing.** An empty list cannot offer a wrong option; channel breakdown comes from the order's own channel, never from a typed category. **The income category field is OPTIONAL and hides entirely when the list is empty** — manual income entry then shows amount, date and note and no category field — while **"add income" stays visible regardless**, never gated behind creating a category first, which would leave a tenant with non-sale money, no route to record it and no sign explaining why. **Also recorded as a standing fact rather than a decision: `routes/finance.js` calls `storeCategory` zero times** and stores category values raw in both directions, with no trim and no normalisation, on a free-text column with no foreign key; Purchasing normalises at PO-line save so PO-derived rows arrive clean, and Finance is the exception. **The three superseded open items are LEFT STANDING** in *Explicitly NOT decided here* rather than struck, on the usual convention; the new subsections supersede them in place, and one new open item is added. Docs only; no code, no schema, no routes.

2026-09-01 · v4.110 — **§36 settles where settlement receipts belong by ruling that they belong nowhere in Finance: revenue comes from the order record, and a platform payout is that same money arriving in the bank.** A sale is counted at the moment the order exists, so recording the payout as income counts the same yuan twice — settlement receipts therefore have no representation in the Finance staircase, no row in Transactions, and no income category. **Transactions keeps exactly two directions; no third "payout" type is added.** **The absence of a category meaning "platform payout" was the original cause of the Mini App mis-filing, and the fix is explicitly NOT to add one** — adding it would turn a one-off mistake into a repeatable, correctly-labelled double-count. **The ¥152,309 filed under Mini App is confirmed as two hand-totalled summaries of daily platform arrivals**, described `6月` and `7月`, plus one real ¥413.30 sale: not monthly transfers, not sales, and only the ¥413.30 is revenue. Settlement receipts belong to settlement reconciliation, attached to the channel connection, not to the Finance staircase. **A second decision corrects a working assumption carried through the Finance design sessions: Meituan settles DAILY, not monthly**, which reshapes the reconciliation already queued on §36 — per channel per day, summing `channel_settle_amount` across that day's orders against the amount that arrived in the bank, so a mismatch localises to one day's orders rather than a month's, which is the practical argument for the daily cadence. **`channel_settle_amount` is 预计 — a forecast, revised on refund, not a bank confirmation** — so the daily check compares a forecast against an actual arrival, and small divergences are expected and are the signal the check exists to surface rather than errors in themselves. **Eleme is explicitly not covered**: its settlement semantics remain unresolved, and the two channels do not even store the field alike — Meituan keeps the latest poll, Eleme the first seen. Reconciliation is not scheduled, designed or built here. **The superseded open item is LEFT STANDING** in *Explicitly NOT decided here* rather than struck, on the same convention that leaves superseded text unedited; the new subsections supersede it in place. Docs only; no code, no schema, no routes.

2026-09-01 · v4.109 — **The export ran, and its receipt corrects two figures §36 asserted a day earlier.** Income landed exactly as predicted — 26 rows, ¥239,841.06, 13 June to 31 July. **Expenses did not: 168 rows against the 92 a survey found on 4 August, and 25 sub-cent rows against 7.** Neither is an error in the export or in the earlier survey; both counts grew because **Purchasing has kept posting expense rows all along**, and each received purchase order can produce another sub-cent value. **The correction that matters is conceptual rather than numerical:** the expense table spans 8 May to 29 August, so about a month of it post-dates the 1 August cutover and is live data rather than history. Tacet counting from 1 August handles it correctly and nothing is broken — but §36 now says plainly that "the kitchen app's ledger" names a table still being written to, so no later session reads it as a closed set. The export itself is recorded with its date, paths, counts and totals.

2026-09-01 · v4.108 — **§36 sets a cutover: Tacet's Finance counts from 1 August 2026, the kitchen app's ledger is exported to a file, and nothing is deleted.** Established by reading live data rather than by preference. 2026-09-01 · v4.107 — **§36 settles category normalisation: Finance calls `storeCategory` on every write, and the existing rows are corrected once.** Purchasing normalises earlier in the chain — `storeCategory` runs when a PO line's expense category is saved, so `postPOExpenses()` copies an already-normalised value — while Finance has no such upstream step and no `category-text` import at all, so three rent payments typed by three people can land as three categories differing by an invisible Kangxi radical or by ASCII spacing. **The failure mode is the dangerous kind:** Summary's breakdown then draws ¥8,000, ¥12,000 and ¥6,000 as three identical-looking lines instead of one ¥26,000 line, so the total is right, every line beneath it is wrong, and nothing on screen looks broken. **Normalise-on-read was rejected** because it leaves storage dirty, making correctness depend on every future reader remembering — one that forgets reintroduces the fault silently — and because Transactions lists rows rather than grouping them, so the operator would still face rows they cannot tell apart. **The one-time pass is treated as what it is, a script that edits live financial data:** category text only, never an amount or a date, with a backup immediately before and a dry run read by a person first. `scripts/normalise_finance_categories.js` already exists and is the starting point. **The open item is REPLACED, not closed** — income categories live in browser localStorage and have never been synced to the server, so normalising them yields consistent values and still no shared list; where they should live is a Settings question. Three open items remain on §36.

2026-08-27 · v4.99 — **DAMAGE ON A DELIVERY IS A MONEY QUESTION, NOT A STOCK QUESTION, RECORDED AS §35.** A NEW DECISION THAT REVERSES NO EARLIER RULE — it settles what happens to the VALUE of damaged units, which the record had never ruled on, and no existing § is narrowed, withdrawn or contradicted by it. Every damaged quantity now carries an outcome the operator chooses when the damage is recorded — **REPLACING**, **CREDITED** or **UNRESOLVED** — and there is no default that resolves itself. **THE THREE OUTCOMES DIFFER IN WHAT IS OWED AND WHETHER THE ORDER IS DONE.** REPLACING leaves the amount owed unchanged and the order open until the replacements arrive; CREDITED drops the amount owed by the damaged units' value and completes the delivery; UNRESOLVED holds that value — neither owed nor written off — and leaves the order open. **NO ACCOUNT IS FORCED INTO ONE OUTCOME.** A business whose suppliers always replace picks REPLACING every time at the cost of one click, a business whose suppliers always credit picks CREDITED, and neither is the product's assumption or hardcoded — §0 governs, and a rule that only fits one supplier relationship is not a rule. **AN ORDER DOES NOT CLOSE WHILE GOODS ARE OWED**: REPLACING or UNRESOLVED damage keeps it open, because an order that closes with units outstanding is an order nobody chases. **WHAT THIS SECTION DOES NOT REOPEN: damaged units never enter stock**, under any outcome. That is unchanged from current behaviour — §34's key is untouched and the exclusion at receiving time stands — and it is restated inside §35 only so the new outcomes are not misread as putting some of them back. **RENUMBERING: Related documents moves from §35 to §36** so the reference appendix stays last, the shape v4.97 established. One live pointer followed it — v4.92's entry, which cites the waste-survey line as §35's, now reads §36. v4.97's own record of the earlier §34/§35 swap is left exactly as written: like v4.92's "moves from §33 to §34" sentence, it is a dated account of a past move, not a claim about where anything lives today.

2026-08-27 · v4.98 — **§33's BODY STOPS CITING THE WRONG SECTION: "READING §34 AS A RESTATEMENT OF §29" NOW READS §33.** A CORRECTION OF A PRE-EXISTING WRONG CROSS-REFERENCE, and the only change in this version — no decision is made, narrowed, withdrawn or reversed, and no section moves. The closing sentence of §33's fourth paragraph is **§33 describing itself**: the paragraph opens "This is adjacent to §29's rule and is NOT an amendment to it" and argues that destroyed is a third case §29's sold-or-consumed rule does not answer, so the section the reader must not mistake for a restatement of §29 is the one they are reading. **IT POINTED AT THE WRONG SECTION BOTH BEFORE AND AFTER v4.97.** The number was already wrong when it was written — §34 was Related documents, a list of files, which cannot restate anything — and v4.97's swap moved it onto the stock-key decision, wrong in a new way rather than newly wrong. v4.97 left it deliberately and said so, because correcting it changes meaning and does not belong in a renumbering entry; this entry is where it belongs. **THE SAME STRING IN v4.97's ENTRY IS NOT TOUCHED**: that entry quotes the defective sentence verbatim to record what was left alone on the day, and a quotation of an error is not the error.

2026-08-27 · v4.97 — **§34 AND §35 SWAP PLACES: THE STOCK-KEY DECISION BECOMES §34, RELATED DOCUMENTS BECOMES §35.** A RENUMBERING ONLY — NEITHER SECTION'S CONTENT OR MEANING CHANGES BY ONE WORD, and no decision is made, narrowed, withdrawn or reversed here. Stock is counted by item and place — nothing else, added as §35 in v4.96, moves ahead of Related documents and is now **§34**; Related documents moves to the end of the file and is now **§35**. **WHY: A REFERENCE APPENDIX BELONGS LAST.** Related documents is a list of other files, not a decision, and v4.96 appended a decision behind it by following the file's numbering rather than its shape; the decisions now run unbroken from §0 to §34 with the appendix closing the document. **TWO CROSS-REFERENCES WERE REPOINTED TO FOLLOW THE MOVE** — v4.96's own entry, which recorded the stock decision as §35, now reads §34; and v4.92's entry, which cited the waste-survey line as §34's, now reads §35. **A THIRD `§34` IN §33's BODY WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE**: "Reading §34 as a restatement of §29 gets both wrong" is a pre-existing error that pointed at Related documents before this renumbering and at the stock decision after it, and is self-evidently meant to read §33 — correcting it is a change of meaning and does not belong in a renumbering entry. **SO WAS v4.92's SENTENCE THAT RELATED DOCUMENTS "MOVES FROM §33 TO §34"**, which is a dated record of what that entry did on the day, not a pointer to where anything lives now; the two numbers in it describe a past move and stay as written. Only pointers were repointed — history was not rewritten.

2026-08-27 · v4.96 — **STOCK IS KEYED ON ITEM AND LOCATION AND NOTHING ELSE, RECORDED AS §34.** A NEW DECISION THAT REVERSES NO EARLIER RULE — it settles a dimension the record had simply never ruled on, and no existing § is narrowed, withdrawn or contradicted by it. A stock quantity has exactly two parts: the item, and the location it sits in. There is no third part — not purpose, not department, not intended use, not kitchen-versus-retail. **AN ITEM DOES NOT KNOW WHERE IT IS GOING.** The same item may be consumed in production, sold on a shelf, listed on a sales channel, or all three; nothing on the item record decides which. The destination is named by a purchase line, never implied by the kind of item, so any code or screen that reads a destination off an item's type is wrong. **A BUSINESS THAT WANTS TWO COUNTS OF ONE ITEM CREATES TWO LOCATIONS.** A kitchen and a shopfront at one street address are two locations, and so are two shelves in one room; a location is whatever the business says it is, and the system does not check that locations are physically distinct. That path is always available and needs no feature, setting or flag. **NOT CONFIGURABLE, AND NOTHING IS WITHHELD BY THAT.** A per-account switch between a two-part and a three-part key would force every stock read, write, transfer, count, report and channel sync to carry both shapes permanently; the two-part key is the only shape. **RATIONALE: PURPOSE IS NOT A PROPERTY OF GOODS SITTING ON A SHELF.** It is a decision made when the goods are moved or used. Putting it on the stock row freezes a decision nobody has made yet, and produces counts that disagree the moment someone takes a bag from the wrong pile.

2026-08-27 · v4.95 — **§29 GAINS A FOURTH ADDENDUM: A MATERIALIZED RECIPE'S COST YIELDS TO ITS MATERIAL'S OWN PURCHASE PRICE.** §29's core text says a linked material's cost is derived from its recipe rather than a purchase price — true of a recipe materialized as a brand-new material (`materializeNew()`, no purchase history) and **no longer true once that recipe is instead linked to a material that already had one** (`materializeLink()`, an existing `ingredients` row with its own `buy_price`). This narrows the original sentence rather than reversing it. **RATIONALE: THE MATERIAL WAS BOUGHT, AND THAT IS WHAT IT COST.** Where a recipe and a bought material are the same physical thing, the recipe describes what was done to it — repacked, portioned, relabelled — not where it came from; costing the event from the recipe instead of the purchase would price a bag of bought powder by what the kitchen scale says rather than what the supplier invoiced. **NOT A HYPOTHETICAL — IT IS THE PATTERN A SAME-DAY READ-ONLY AUDIT SURFACED.** Running `ensureMaterialized()`'s exact check across all 137 recipes (no writes) found 16 that would collide with an existing, unlinked material; 11 are one repeated shape — a recipe named identically to a bought raw material, the Organic Powder family plus Sumac, Extra Virgin Coconut Oil and Coconut Flakes — plus BioCurcumin+ (Organic) colliding on SKU rather than name. Once a human links one of those to its bought material, the rollup must not then quietly replace the supplier's price with the recipe's. **THE DETECTION MECHANISM IS DELIBERATELY NOT DECIDED HERE** — `buy_price > 0`, which materialize action made the link, or another signal, is left to whichever PR touches `lib/recipe-rollup.js`'s write path (§4 of the plan, Step 4), the same way the first §29 addendum deferred its own mechanism. **THE 16 COLLISIONS THEMSELVES ARE NOT RESOLVED BY THIS ADDENDUM AND ARE NOT BEING RESOLVED IN CODE** — Ash clears them by hand; this only settles what must happen to cost once one of them is linked. A narrowing addendum that reverses no rule, hence a patch. Docs only; no code changed.

2026-08-27 · v4.94 — **§31 GAINS AN ADDENDUM: A BUILD LINE IS THE PRODUCT'S ONLY COST SOURCE. §29 GAINS A THIRD: SAVING A RECIPE ALWAYS MATERIALIZES ITS OUTPUT.** Two decisions closing the two open questions `docs/tacet-product-build-lines-design.md` (Step 1 of the product bill-of-materials build) raised rather than guessed at. **FIRST: ONCE A PRODUCT HAS A BUILD LIST, `store_products.recipe_id` IS NOT CONSULTED FOR COST BY ANYTHING.** The two do not coexist — a product has exactly one cost source, and the reason is §29's own: a target that could be either of two things means every reader handles two cases, the same shape that produced five divergent copies of the recipe cost formula before §29 closed it at the recipe-line level. A recipe's output already reaches a product the same way a box or a label does — as a material, via a build line — so there was never a second path that needed keeping; `recipe_id` narrows to the one job unaffected by cost, the allergen rollup in `routes/products.js`. **SECOND: MATERIALIZATION STOPS BEING OPT-IN.** Live at 28 of 137 active recipes today, reached only through the human-triggered `POST .../materialize` — a hard dependency the design doc surfaced, not a nice-to-have, because a build line cannot point at a made thing's cost until that thing has a materials row. Saving a recipe now creates or updates its row every time, whether or not anything uses it yet, closing the gap for the other 109. **THE NAME-COLLISION QUESTION THIS REOPENS IS NAMED AND EXPLICITLY NOT ANSWERED HERE** — the first §29 addendum already found none of the platform's three signals for telling a legacy made row from a legacy bought one trustworthy alone or in combination, and settled that a human resolved all 40 of Roots' real collisions; automatic materialization creates a new instance of the identical question, on every future save rather than as a one-time migration, and it is deferred to the PR that builds it on the same terms the first addendum already set — surfaced for a human, never resolved by guessing. **Two other points from the same review are recorded as CONFIRMED rather than reopened**: the 171-row cost-population pass stays out of scope for the four remaining build steps, a separate operational pass after the screen ships; and the `product_build_lines` table, the cost roll-up split (`lib/ingredient-cost.js` unchanged, `lib/recipe-cost.js`'s `buildLines()` exported rather than duplicated), and folding the recompute into the existing `fireRecompute`/`applyRollup` network are all approved as designed. Neither addendum reverses a rule; both narrow an open question to a decision. Evidence: `docs/tacet-product-build-lines-design.md`, all seven sections. Docs only; no code changed.

2026-08-27 · v4.93 — **§31 RULE 2'S HUMMUS ASLI EXAMPLE IS WITHDRAWN: IT IS NOT AN INSTANCE OF THAT RULE, AND ITS TWO FIGURES WERE UNSOURCED.** Rule 2 says packaging is chosen on the PRODUCT because one recipe backs several products packed differently, and it offered Hummus Asli as "the same shape at scale" — six products at four price points on one recipe carrying a single 300ml box. **Both halves of that sentence are wrong, and they are wrong in opposite directions.** There is not one Hummus Asli recipe but TWO — 7 (SKU 1-12) and 92 (SKU 1-10) — sharing both `name_en` and `name_cn` and differing only by SKU; the recipe-linking rule at `database.js:4263` requires two of three signals to agree, SKU can therefore serve for neither, both must match on both names, and the family is ambiguous. **So its products are not packed differently off one recipe — they hold NO RECIPE LINK AT ALL**, skipped silently at `:4332` into a counter printed as "skipped N ambiguous". **That makes Hummus Asli rules 7 and 8's case, not rule 2's**: it is precisely the product with packaging and no recipe those rules exist to keep reachable, which is why citing it under rule 2 misfiled the one example that proves the governing constraint. **And the "single 300ml box" was never this recipe's** — recipe 7 carries `packaging_type_id` `'pt1778315688913'`, a client-generated string in an `INTEGER` column matching no `packaging_types` row (finding 7); the 300ml box belongs to recipe 9 (`docs/packaging-findings.md:314-315`). **THE SIX-PRODUCTS-AT-FOUR-PRICE-POINTS FIGURE IS REMOVED AS UNSOURCED RATHER THAN CORRECTED**, and the removal is noted in rule 2 itself so a later reader does not restore it believing it was mislaid — no query was ever behind it. **Crunchy Granola remains rule 2's only worked example, and it is unaffected.** Recorded in full as `docs/packaging-findings.md` **finding 18**, which also marks UNVERIFIED that recipes 7 and 92 both still exist and still share both names — `database.js:4267` is a claim made when that migration was written, not a live read — and states plainly that the underlying defect is one of recipe IDENTITY rather than of packaging, filed there only because §31's example surfaced it. **A SECOND UNSOURCED FIGURE IS RECORDED WITHOUT BEING CHANGED: the "65 products" in §31's consequences.** It appears only in §31 (`:4244`) and in v4.88's entry above, with no measured source, and the operative number is smaller than 65 in any case — a product already showing an em dash for want of a sell price has no margin to move whichever packaging is picked, and it is that smaller number the rule 9 unknown-state rendering decision turns on. `docs/packaging-findings.md` **finding 19** carries both read-only queries and the warning that the population must be pinned first — archived in or out, and whether `packaging = 0` counts as needing the pass. **65 IS LEFT STANDING IN §31 UNTIL SOMEONE RUNS THEM**, because replacing an unsourced number with a second unsourced number is not an improvement. A correction that withdraws one worked example and reverses no rule — the nine rules are untouched — hence a patch. Docs only; no code changed.

2026-08-27 · v4.92 — **WHETHER A WASTED ITEM'S PACKAGING IS LOST IS RECORDED AS §33: AN ACCOUNT POLICY, NOT A PLATFORM RULE — AND IT IS HARDCODED TWICE TODAY WITH OPPOSITE VALUES.** **Neither answer may be hardcoded, because both businesses are real**: a shop that packs at the point of sale and bins the container with the product has genuinely lost that packaging, and a kitchen discarding unpacked prep has lost none. §0 does not permit picking one and being wrong for the other, so **every route that costs waste reads ONE SHARED ACCOUNT-LEVEL SETTING rather than deciding for itself.** **ROOTS' ANSWER IS THAT THE CONTAINER IS LOST — and that is ROOTS' SETTING, not the platform default**, and must not reach the code as a constant. **THIS IS ADJACENT TO §29's SECOND ADDENDUM AND IS NOT AN AMENDMENT TO IT.** That rule governs two ways a thing leaves — SOLD, or CONSUMED by another recipe — and settles that packaging belongs to the serving that is sold. **DESTROYED IS A THIRD CASE AND NEITHER OF THE FIRST TWO ANSWERS IT**: a container that does not travel to a consumer may still be lost when the unit holding it is binned, and §29's reasoning about reused kitchen tubs says nothing about a sellable unit thrown away in its packaging. Reading §33 as a restatement of §29 gets both wrong. **🔴 RECORDED AS A LIVE DEFECT, NOT A DESIGN: THE POLICY IS HARDCODED IN TWO PLACES WITH OPPOSITE VALUES AND BOTH ARE IN PRODUCTION.** The kitchen route EXCLUDES the parent recipe's packaging (`routes/waste.js:56`), reasoning in the file that a container is recycled onto the replacement unit; the retail route INCLUDES it, reading `store_products.unit_cost`, which the cascade writes as `costPerServing` and which contains `packagingTotal`. **Both are mounted in the same process, so the same wasted item costs differently depending on which route recorded it.** Under Roots' policy the retail route is correct and the kitchen route understates a loss — but **the divergence is wrong under either policy**, because one of the two is always wrong and nothing reconciles them. **IT WAS NEVER A DECISION**: nothing in the retail route argues that a wasted product incurs its packaging and nothing acknowledges the kitchen route's recycled-container reasoning. It arrived as a consequence of reading a stored column — which is what §32 rule 5 asks for and what §31 rule 1 establishes that column to contain. **Both rules were followed and the question was never put**, which is recorded so the fix is understood as settling a question nobody asked rather than reversing a considered choice. **REACHABLE IN PRODUCTION**, which is why it carries a defect marker rather than sitting in Open questions: both routes deployed at run 1415, the feature gate defaults ON when its config row is absent, and the capabilities are granted to existing store-manager and warehouse roles. **ONE QUESTION IS DELIBERATELY NOT DESIGNED: whether the policy should turn on whether the item had actually been PACKED when it was wasted** — a finished unit binned in its jar and a tray of prep binned before it was ever packed are different events, no field records that today, and **it must not be built on until it is asked for**, since a per-event packed flag is a larger change than the setting this rule requires. The setting's name, where it lives, its default for a new account and how the two routes are brought onto it are all left to the build. §37's waste-survey entry also gains the note that §32 is now built and live. Related documents moves from §33 to §34; nothing cross-references either number. A new decision that reverses no earlier rule and edits no existing section, hence a patch. Docs only; no code changed.

2026-08-27 · v4.91 — **§32 GAINS AN ADDENDUM: THE MATERIAL SUBJECT IS DEFERRED, THE BUSINESS DATE ANCHORS ON THE LOCATION, AND COST STORES A RESOLVED TOTAL.** Three decisions made when the first build against §32 was scoped, and made because that build **stopped before anything was written** rather than choosing its way past them — which is the reason they are decisions rather than defaults discovered later in a diff. **RULES 3, 6 AND 12 ARE NOT REWRITTEN AND NOTHING IS EDITED AWAY**; point 2 changes what rule 12 resolves against and says so in place. **THE MATERIAL SUBJECT IS DEFERRED, NOT DROPPED.** Materials have no stock and no ledger — no stock column on the master, no material stock table — and **§31 rule 6 records that as a DECISION rather than a gap**, so it cannot be treated as an oversight to patch around; rules 3 and 6 therefore cannot both hold for a material subject, one requiring the subject to be a material or a product and the other requiring the record to move stock there is none of. **The resolution is that the record's SHAPE is unchanged** — subject type, both nullable keys, exactly one set — **and the material subject is refused at the API until material stock exists.** Rule 3's purpose was to stop two features being built here and **that purpose is served by the shape, not by shipping both subjects together**: one table, one constraint, one code path, one of its two subjects not yet accepted. **Rule 6 holds unbroken, because nothing without stock can be recorded at all.** **Material waste unblocks when material stock is designed, which is its own decision and must not be smuggled into a waste build.** **THE BUSINESS DATE RESOLVES FROM THE LOCATION, NOT THE ACCOUNT** — rule 12 says the account's zone, there is no account zone in the schema and there is a per-location one, and **the location is the better anchor regardless of what exists**: waste always occurs somewhere, so the place it happened is a fact about the event rather than a setting standing in for one, and an account spanning two zones would otherwise date a loss by neither. Rule 12 now reads that the business date is resolved in the time zone of the LOCATION the waste occurred at, falling back to the system default where a location has none; the rest of it stands, including its subjection to §0. **COST IS STORED AS A RESOLVED TOTAL IN WHOLE CENTS**, computed once at entry as unit cost times quantity and rounded there — **§24's exclusion of whole cents for per-unit costs applies to RATES that get multiplied downstream**, where a per-gram figure rounded to a cent and multiplied by a thousand carries the error a thousand times, and **this is the product of that multiplication, already resolved, with nothing downstream multiplying it again**. It does not reopen §24 and does not generalise beyond this column. **ONE THING IS RECORDED AS OPEN AND EXPLICITLY NOT RESOLVED: §24's money rule names an arbiter that no longer exists.** MONEY IS RESOLVED BY SCHEMA CLASS, NEVER BY COLUMN NAME defines a money column as one `scripts/postgres-full-copy/plan.json` classes CENTS or NUM6 and says **no other test is permitted** — and that file was deleted with the cancelled Postgres migration, so **the rule cannot be applied by anyone in either direction**: no permitted way to establish that a column is money, and none to establish that it is not. It is wider than waste, it reaches every future money column, and it needs its own pass; the cost decision above settles one column on its own reasoning and deliberately does not stand in for the general answer. An addendum answering questions §32 left to its build, reversing nothing and editing no rule away, hence a patch. Docs only; no code changed.

2026-08-27 · v4.90 — **§32's evidence is listed where §30's and §31's are.** `docs/tacet-waste-survey.md` joins Related documents, immediately after `docs/packaging-findings.md`, so the three decision sections written from surveys have their evidence contiguous rather than one of them reachable only from the section that cites it. **The entry records what the survey establishes and what it refused to establish**: one table, one route file, one screen; products only and no stock movement; the recipe-then-sell-price costing that made Recipes look like a Phase 1 dependency; H1, the kitchen-catalogue product reference that decided §32 rule 2; and the four questions marked UNVERIFIED because no database was opened. 2026-08-27 · v4.89 — **WASTE IS RECORDED AS §32: A STOCK MOVEMENT WITH A REASON, NOT A FEATURE OF ITS OWN.** Thirteen decisions, stated as intent and naming no table, column, screen or function, like §30's and §31's. **WASTE IS NOT A FEATURE, IT IS A REASON** — stock going down for any cause that is not a sale is ONE mechanism, and waste is one of the reasons it records; the kitchen app's waste screen is a log that moves no stock, and **that is a defect rather than a model to port**, because a business can record fifty units lost and still be offering all fifty for sale on every channel. **THE KITCHEN WASTE SCREEN IS NOT MIGRATED, IT IS REPLACED**: `waste_entries` is not back-migrated, the three live rows are abandoned, and the kitchen screen stays live until Roots is cut over and is then retired. **That deliberately abandons history and the reason is recorded so it is not later met as an oversight** — the table holds three rows and its `product_id` points at the KITCHEN products table rather than the store catalogue, which is the survey's H1 id-space hazard, so building fresh against `store_products` removes the hazard where back-migrating three rows would carry it in. **ONE MECHANISM, TWO SUBJECTS** — a waste record's subject is either a MATERIAL or a PRODUCT, **a field and not a fork, and two features must never be built here**; exactly one of the two is set on any row, and §21's separation of Products from Materials is untouched because what is shared is the movement, not the master. **THE MATERIAL SUBJECT REQUIRES THE PRODUCTION MODULE AND THE PRODUCT SUBJECT DOES NOT** — a pure retail account that makes nothing still wastes finished stock, so **waste carries its own account-level toggle and is not gated behind Production**. **RECIPES ARE NOT A DEPENDENCY**: a product's cost is the stored scalar on the product, a material's cost is its own stored cost, and **this closes the dependency the survey raised against §28's Phase 1 boundary** — the kitchen implementation costs a wasted product through its recipe and falls back to the SELL PRICE when it cannot, which books a loss at retail and needs the Recipes work §28 defers. **RECORDING WASTE MOVES STOCK** — it writes a stock ledger row and the on-hand number goes down, because a loss that leaves the number unchanged records nothing and forces a second manual adjustment that will sometimes not happen; the ledger already reserves `waste` as a reason value and nothing writes it today, which is the defect in one line. **REASON CODES ARE MANDATORY**, a quantity with no reason being unable to answer the only question worth asking — whether less should have been made — and **the seeded set is fixed in this phase and not account-editable**: spoiled, expired, damaged, preparation error, staff consumption, sampling, other, with `other` requiring a note. **A DISCOUNTED SALE IS NOT WASTE** — unsold stock sold cheap at close is REVENUE and belongs in Orders and must never be recordable as waste, since recording it as one understates takings and overstates spoilage so the two errors hide each other; **stock taken by staff is a real cost but a different one** and gets its own reason code rather than being folded into spoilage. **COST IS SNAPSHOT AT ENTRY AND NEVER RECOMPUTED** — a later price change must not restate a past loss. **NO COST AVAILABLE IS NOT ZERO COST**: the row saves, cost is stored as absent, the row is flagged UNCOSTED, and reports show the count of uncosted rows alongside the total rather than silently understating the loss — **storing zero, which is today's behaviour, is a defect**, and it is §31 rule 9's unknown-is-not-zero applied to a movement instead of a master record. **ENTRIES ARE NEVER EDITED OR DELETED** — a mistake is VOIDED, writing a reversal row and returning the stock, per §20; stated here only because the kitchen implementation hard-deletes and keeps no record of what the deleted row said. **DATES RESOLVE IN THE ACCOUNT'S TIME ZONE** — the survey found every date on the waste path is UTC while the business runs at UTC+8, so a loss recorded before eight in the morning lands on the previous day. **A CLOSE ROUTINE IS A SEPARATE, LATER PIECE OF WORK** — an end-of-day sweep listing a location's perishable products is how the number becomes RELIABLE rather than merely available, but it is a screen writing these same rows and it needs a perishable flag that does not exist, so it is deliberately not in this phase and **building this phase must not make it harder**. **THREE THINGS ARE RECORDED AS OPEN AND DEFERRED RATHER THAN DECIDED**: whether reason codes become account-editable, whether waste feeds a production or purchasing signal, and the perishable flag. The evidence — the three live rows, the id-space hazard, the sell-price fallback, the UTC dates, the silent zero-cost save and the unused ledger reason — is `docs/tacet-waste-survey.md` and deliberately NOT restated here. Related documents moves from §32 to §33; nothing cross-references either number. A new decision that reverses no earlier rule and edits no existing section, hence a patch. Docs only; no code changed.

2026-08-26 · v4.88 — **PRODUCT UNIT COST IS RECORDED AS §31: CONTENTS PLUS PACKAGING, AND PACKAGING ATTACHES TO THE PRODUCT.** Nine rules, stated as intent and naming no table, column, screen or function, like §30's. **It is its own section rather than a §29 addendum, and the reason is the reason for the decision.** §29 is about the recipe graph — a made thing is a material, a recipe line points at exactly one target, and its second addendum settles which of a recipe's costs travel along that line. This settles what a PRODUCT costs, and its governing rule is that the packaging half must be reachable with no recipe anywhere in the picture; filing it inside §29 would put a rule whose whole point is that it does not depend on recipes inside the section about recipes, and §29 closes by saying recipes are not connected to retail Products in this phase. **A product's unit cost is its contents plus its packaging, contents coming from a recipe, a purchase price or a figure typed directly, and NEITHER HALF IS MANDATORY.** **PACKAGING IS CHOSEN ON THE PRODUCT, NOT ON THE RECIPE**, because one recipe backs several products packed differently — Crunchy Granola is a ¥43 jar and an ¥8 sample pack from one recipe, and the sample pack is deliberately excluded from recipe-linking today because the model has nowhere to put its own container; Hummus Asli is six products at four price points on one recipe carrying a single 300ml box. **A PRODUCT CARRIES A LIST OF PACKAGING MATERIALS, NOT ONE** — Roots packs a jar, a sticker and a label, the model records one, and the other two are not costed at all. **That is not a variant problem and not a future one: it is wrong on ordinary flat products right now, and real packaging cost is understated by it.** **PACKAGING IS A MATERIAL LIKE ANY OTHER** — already bought, priced and recorded as one, and the standalone packaging list duplicates the same physical object with a hand-typed price whose entries have already drifted from what was paid. One record per physical thing. **THE RECIPE CARRIES NO PACKAGING**: a recipe is what it costs to make the food, which is also exactly what a sub-recipe needs when it feeds another recipe, so this makes visible in the screens the separation `c86ef74e` made in the numbers. **PACKAGING DOES NOT DEPLETE STOCK** — Ash's decision, recorded as a decision rather than left looking like an omission, because nothing depletes any material today and an omission invites a later reader to "fix" it. **NOTHING IN THE PACKAGING HALF MAY ASSUME A KITCHEN** — no servings, no batch sizes — and **THIS IS THE GOVERNING CONSTRAINT THAT OUTRANKS THE REST**: any business in any country must be able to use Tacet (§0), and a shop bagging almonds or a butcher wrapping a tray has packaging and no kitchen, so a model reachable only through a recipe locks those tenants out entirely rather than merely inconveniencing them. **A PRODUCT WITH NO RECIPE CAN STILL HAVE PACKAGING** — the reseller case, and why the design generalises. **AN EMPTY PACKAGING LIST MEANS UNKNOWN, NOT ZERO** — Ash's decision: a missing figure is a hard zero today, so a product nobody has filled in looks identical to one that genuinely has no packaging and reports a margin that is too good; unknown makes the one-time migration pass visible, and there must be an explicit way to say "no packaging" so the reseller selling loose goods is correct rather than merely unfinished. **THREE THINGS ARE RECORDED AS CONSEQUENCES AND NOT AS DECISIONS**: costs will RISE where packaging was under-counted, which is the opposite direction from `c86ef74e` and has the same purpose — both make the number honest; **65 products carry a packaging figure through their recipe and each needs its packaging picked once**, and that one-time pass is the real cost of this change rather than the code; and a gift box holding several different products is a finished good with no recipe that references other PRODUCTS rather than materials, recorded as a known limit of this design and explicitly not solved here. **THE SCHEMA, THE SCREENS AND THE MIGRATION ARE DELIBERATELY NOT DESIGNED** — this settles what is true, and how it is built comes later and must answer to these rules. The evidence — packaging living on the recipe with no product column, the standalone table's 44 rows and 8 drifted pairs, the hard zero, and nothing depleting any material — is `docs/packaging-findings.md` findings 2, 3, 4, 6, 9 and 12, and deliberately NOT restated here. Related documents moves from §31 to §32; nothing cross-references either number. A new decision that reverses no earlier rule, hence a patch. Docs only; no code changed.

2026-08-26 · v4.87 — **§6 GAINS A SECOND ADDENDUM: WHAT BECOMES OF A RECIPE THAT CANNOT DERIVE, AND WHICH FIGURE GOVERNS UNTIL IT CAN.** The first addendum made servings derived and left two questions it did not have to answer at the time: what happens to a recipe that cannot produce a derived figure, and which of the three existing numbers wins where they disagree. **Both were settled from a survey of LIVE DATA before any build began, not from the model.** What the survey found is why the rule reads as it does: batch size, servings and serving size are three independently typed fields with nothing reconciling them; **servings is the number the system actually trusts**, because production logs multiply it by batch count; **serving size is inert** — stored, displayed, and read by no derivation at all; and **23 of 137 live recipes carry no servings figure**. **DERIVING REQUIRES A SERVING SIZE, AND ABSENT ONE THE STORED SERVINGS STANDS.** The recipe keeps its typed figure, that figure stays authoritative, and the recipe is marked UNCONVERTED — not blanked, not guessed at, and not derived from a serving size invented to make the sum work. **An unconverted recipe blocks batch-size auto-fill exactly as an unconverted unit line does**, which is deliberate rather than convenient: one unconverted state with two causes — a missing density under the §7 addendum, or a missing serving size here — with the screen naming which, so an operator does not learn two vocabularies for one situation. **NOTHING IS RECOSTED WITHOUT AN OPERATOR ACTING**, and the reason is sharper than it was a day ago: cost per serving now paints on open rather than on the first keystroke (`6d26a0f7`), so a figure that moved would move in front of an operator who did not ask for it — and cost per serving reaches product cost and therefore margin. Where all three figures exist and disagree, stored servings governs until someone sets the serving size on that recipe, per recipe, by hand, with no deadline and no bulk script. **ZERO SERVINGS IS NOT A VALUE** — zero means "computed to zero" where absent means "not yet known", only absent is meaningful, zero is unreachable through any interface and no live recipe holds one, and it must not return as a sentinel, a default, or a cleared-field value. **A CONSUMER OF THE CHANGING NUMBER IS NAMED SO IT IS NOT MET LATE**: `routes/production.js` multiplies stored servings by batch count to record what was made, and must be checked against the derived figure BEFORE servings becomes derived anywhere, not after. Subject to §0: a tenant whose recipes yield counts rather than portions has no serving size to record and is permanently and legitimately unconverted — **unconverted is a resting state, not a fault, and must never be presented as an error.** §6's existing rules and the first addendum are both untouched. An addendum answering questions an earlier addendum left open, reversing and contradicting nothing, hence a patch. Docs only; no code changed.

2026-08-26 · v4.86 — **§29 GAINS A RULE: A COST DERIVED FROM MAKING A THING IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY A COST OF USING IT.** §29 made a made thing a material and settled that a recipe line points at exactly one target. What it did not settle is WHICH OF A RECIPE'S COSTS TRAVEL with that material, and the gap was live: packaging was counted twice on every recipe consuming a made material. **The kitchen reality decided it, not the arithmetic.** A batch is part-sold as retail units in serving-sized containers and part-held in bulk for later use as a material; the bulk half goes into reused kitchen tubs that are not a tracked cost. So the retail container belongs to the sellable unit and must not travel. **LABOUR AND OVERHEAD TRAVEL, PACKAGING DOES NOT** — labour on a bulk batch is work genuinely performed and the parent is consuming its product. **Neither labour nor overhead is in live use today** (one recipe carries them and it backs no material), so settling them costs nothing now and settles them before they matter. **OVERHEAD IS EXPLICITLY NOT FINISHED**, and this rule must not be read as having closed it: overhead is a PERCENTAGE OF INGREDIENT COST, so a parent applying its own overhead to a line that already carries the child's COMPOUNDS rather than duplicates. That is a different fault from this one, nothing exercises it today, and it needs its own answer. **WHICH COSTS TRAVEL IS A PROPERTY OF THE COST, NOT OF THE RECIPE** — deciding it once per cost type is cheaper than deciding it per recipe forever, and it is the decision that actually unblocks a fix. **AND THE EXCLUSION BELONGS WHERE THE MATERIAL'S UNIT COST IS DERIVED, NOT WHERE A PARENT READS IT** — waste costing already sets that precedent by excluding packaging at the consumer, and doing the same here would make every consumer re-decide; deriving it once means one place. That is also why the implementation is a declared table of which components travel rather than a subtraction at the one call site: the next cost under question would otherwise land as a second subtraction in a second place with its own arithmetic, and "which costs travel" would have two answers that drift. **A SIDE EFFECT WORTH RECORDING: this repairs waste costing, which was already trying to do the right thing and being defeated.** Waste deliberately rebuilds a packaging-free batch total, but a made material arrived inside the ingredient subtotal with packaging already folded in, so the exclusion was bypassed on 11 recipes. It now holds. The evidence — the mechanism in three lines of code, the eleven materials, the sixteen lines, and the worked example reconciling to `store_products.unit_cost` to the digit — is finding 1 in `docs/packaging-findings.md` and deliberately NOT restated here. A new rule that reverses no earlier decision, hence a patch. **Code changed: `lib/recipe-cost.js` + `lib/recipe-rollup.js`.**

2026-08-26 · v4.85 — **§30 RULE 3 MOVES FROM THE CALLERS TO THE WRITE, AND §30 RULE 7 GETS ITS FIRST PARTIAL IMPLEMENTATION.** The rules are UNTOUCHED; this records an instance and a fix. **The general shape, which is not channel-specific: a rule enforced by the callers of a write is a convention, and a convention is declined by whichever caller nobody checked.** Here the rule "a value binding our record to an external system is selected from values that system supplied" was enforced in the browser by two separate client gates, both correct, and by nothing underneath them. **The caller that declined it was not the one anyone suspected.** The screen refuses a TYPED name that its catalogue does not hold; what it cannot refuse is a catalogue that a person filled in — the paste escape hatch assigns pasted text into the client-side list, after which every client check agrees the pasted string came from the channel, because on the client it now did. 138 mappings were written that way in under four minutes on 2026-06-22, one of them onto a name the store has never reported, which then failed every two hours for two months. **The fix reads a table the operator cannot write to** — only the scraping daemon fills it — so the property holds for every caller, including ones not yet written. No override, no force flag: a name that cannot be verified is refused. **TWO REFUSALS, NOT ONE, and the distinction is §30 rule 4 rather than ergonomics**: "this name is not in the catalogue" is a verdict about the name, and "this store has no catalogue" is a check that could not run, and reporting the second as the first tells an operator their correct name is wrong. **Clearing is NOT gated, and the ordering is load-bearing**: an empty name is a removal rather than a claim about a listing, and gating it would make the one row that fails the check unremovable — a fault that traps its own subject is worse than the one it replaces. **The gate is WRITE-TIME ONLY, with no sweep**: 393 of 394 stored names re-save cleanly, the one that does not keeps its value untouched and is refused only on the next write of it, and if the channel lists that name again the same write is accepted. **A REMEDY MUST NOT BE THE ACTION THAT WAS REFUSED** — the catalogue could previously only be refreshed by running the matcher, which is the thing now gated, so the refresh became its own control that applies nothing. **Rule 7 is now PARTLY met on this channel and the remaining gap is named rather than glossed**: the change, the previous value, the new value and the operator are recorded, but whether a matcher or a person chose the name is CALLER-DECLARED, because nothing server-side can tell them apart — a claim in the trail, not a fact, and recorded as such so a later reader does not treat it as evidence. **A pre-existing audit fault is written down and explicitly NOT fixed**: tenant and kitchen user ids are separate sequences that collide, so an audit row can carry one person's id beside another person's username; read the username, never the id. It affects every route that logs from the tenant realm and belongs to shared middleware. **And a correction: the finding that prompted this was wrong about which caller was open, in a way that reached the brief that commissioned the fix.** The fix was right and its stated reason was not; both the error and its propagation are marked in place in `docs/meituan-findings.md` finding 11 rather than folded away. The evidence — the two refusal codes, the paste mechanism, the 393/394 split, the audit fields and the id collision — is findings 11 and 12 in that document and deliberately NOT restated here. An instance and a fix that reverse no earlier decision, hence a patch. **Code changed: `d7848b62`.**

2026-08-26 · v4.84 — **§7 gains an addendum: no conversion without a stated factor.** §7 already requires a per-material ml-to-gram conversion and already says it differs per material, and it has never said what happens when that figure is absent — so the absent case was being answered in the only way an unstated case ever is, by a silent fallback, and the fallback was one millilitre to one gram. **That is true for water and for nothing else**, and it was applied to every liquid: the weight of oils understated, the weight of syrups overstated, in both directions without a mark. The addendum records the refusal rather than the guess. **CONVERSIONS ARE OF TWO KINDS AND MUST NOT BE TREATED ALIKE** — same-dimension conversions (kilograms to grams, pounds to ounces, litres to millilitres) are fixed constants true for every material, which the system supplies and nobody enters; cross-dimension conversions (volume to weight) require a DENSITY, and density is a property of the material rather than of the system, so oil, water and syrup differ, there is no default, and none may be invented. **A cross-dimension unit is therefore offered only where that material carries a density** — absent one the unit is not in the picker at all, and **new lines lacking it are refused AT THE POINT OF ENTRY rather than at save or at cost time**, so the operator meets the constraint while they can still act on it. **LINES ALREADY RECORDED UNDER THE OLD ASSUMPTION ARE NOT SILENTLY RECOSTED**, which is the decision most likely to be mistaken later for an oversight: they keep their existing cost and are marked unconverted, because recosting them would move product costs and therefore margins with no operator action and no notice, and a wrong figure that is visible is preferable to a corrected figure that moved unannounced. They are corrected by hand, one material at a time, with no deadline. **An unconverted line blocks batch-size auto-fill for its recipe**, identical treatment to the count units of the §6 addendum immediately above — where the sum cannot be trusted no sum is offered and the screen states what is missing — which doubles as the migration worklist, since a recipe that will not auto-fill is a recipe still holding an unconverted line. Subject to §0: grams are Roots' base unit and not Tacet's, and a tenant stocking in pounds enters recipe lines in pounds or ounces for identical behaviour, only the letters differing — the rule is one stocking unit per material and no conversion without a stated factor, never a mandated metric system. §7's existing rules are untouched. An addendum adding rules to a section that was silent on the point, reversing and contradicting nothing, hence a patch. Docs only; no code changed.

2026-08-26 · v4.83 — **§6 gains an addendum: where the fixed output number comes from.** §6 has always said that recipe output is FIXED, and it has never said how that number is arrived at — a gap that was about to be filled by whoever built the production screen first, and then treated as settled because it shipped. The addendum records the derivation. **Batch size is seeded from the recipe's own retained lines and stays editable**, the sum being a suggestion rather than a lock; where an operator overrides it the difference is displayed as yield against inputs, which is the only yield-loss record there is, since the override already carries the information a separate loss field would hold. **Every recipe line carries a RETAINED flag, defaulting to yes, and it governs WEIGHT ONLY** — brewing water, blanching or soaking liquid, and a stock used to hydrate a dough and then thrown away consume stock and cost exactly what they cost, and contribute nothing to the batch. The flag has two positions and no partial-retention percentage, because a fraction nobody can measure honestly is a field nobody will fill in honestly; partial absorption is absorbed by the editable batch size instead. **Packaging lines never count toward batch size**, derived from the material's kind rather than from the flag, so there is no operator decision and no second place to get it wrong — §8 still consumes and costs them exactly as it already states. **Servings is derived rather than typed alongside serving size** — batch size ÷ serving size, ROUNDED DOWN, with the remainder shown — because a part portion cannot be sold and cost per serving must never be understated, which leaves the remainder's cost carried by the sellable servings. **§6'S EXISTING RULES ARE UNTOUCHED**, stated plainly so the addendum is not later read as a revision: output is still FIXED, inputs are still recorded as actually used, and a batch still produces exactly the stated amount. **The addendum defers to §7 rather than working around it** — auto-fill runs only where every retained line shares one unit family, and leaves batch size blank for manual entry with the reason on screen where any retained line is a count unit, because units are never converted at recipe level. Subject to §0: weight-based batch sizing is one shape a business may want, and a business whose recipes yield counts rather than weights must be equally well served, with the retained flag and the derived-servings rule applying unchanged. An addendum adding rules to a section that was silent on the point, reversing and contradicting nothing, hence a patch. Docs only; no code changed.

2026-08-26 · v4.82 — **§30 RULE 5 GETS ITS FIRST WORKED EXAMPLE, AND IT IS THE FIRST CODE CHANGE §30 HAS PRODUCED.** The rules are UNTOUCHED; this records an instance and a fix, not a decision. **An alarm was not merely hard to clear — it could not fire.** One archived product with channel sync left on held a store's chronic-drift alarm latched for 28 days, and because the alarm latches on first fire and short-circuits while latched, no NEW drift on that store could raise one for the whole period. **The mechanism is worth stating in the abstract, because it is not specific to this channel: a level-triggered recovery loop that selects its targets without asking whether they are still in use will keep selecting a target nobody can act on — and where the same read also gates the all-clear, one dead target disables the alarm for everything behind it.** That is rule 5 failing by construction rather than by neglect, and it is a sharper failure than the one rule 5 was written from: there the alarm needed a human with database access to clear it, here nothing could clear it and nothing else could sound it. **The fix is one line** — the sweep's target read now excludes archived products — and the alarm cleared on its own 16 seconds after the daemon restarted, which is the behaviour rule 5 asks for. **TWO THINGS ARE RECORDED AS NOT FIXED**, so neither is met later as a fresh discovery. The dashboard badge does not move: it counts the newest queue row per target, and nothing in the code retires a dead row on Meituan or on Eleme — GZ Grocery does, which is the shape a fix would take. And the same missing filter exists on GZ Grocery's two self-firing loops, where it is less dangerous because that channel targets a stable id the channel supplied rather than a name. **A SECOND FINDING IS RECORDED ALONGSIDE IT AND NOT ACTED ON**: the Meituan screen's "Match names" is a THIRD matcher, distinct from the daemon's and from the Eleme script's, running in the operator's browser with no score and no threshold, auto-applying any unique substring hit with no confirmation — and it is what wrote the mapping in the worked example, onto a name that exists on no listing. It is rule 7's absence again, and rule 3 enforced by one caller rather than by the route beneath it. The evidence — the latch file, the log rows, the before/after selection counts, the press history and the 138-row bulk write — is findings 10 and 11 in `docs/meituan-findings.md` and deliberately NOT restated here. An instance and a fix that reverse no earlier decision, hence a patch. **Code changed: `bc0c6144`, one line in `lib/meituan-drift-sweep.js`.**

2026-08-26 · v4.81 — **§30's CHANNEL ORDERING IS REWRITTEN — MEITUAN FIRST, ELEME SECOND — AND IT NOW SAYS WHAT IT ORDERS BY.** v4.80 below recorded the understatement and left the ordering standing pending a decision; Ash ruled, and this is the rewrite. **The rules are untouched. This is the supporting statement rule 7 defers to, not a rule.** **The order is Meituan, Eleme, 闪购, GZ Grocery**, and **it orders by STANDING EXPOSURE — how many of our mappings are one external edit away from a silent wrong write, and whether anything downstream would catch one.** It does NOT order by how badly a matching rule could misbehave in the abstract, and **the basis is now in the text** because that is the third correction and the one that stops this recurring: the old line said "ordering of exposure" and left the word to the reader, and on one honest reading of it Eleme still ranked first. **Two facts moved the order, neither of them a change of opinion.** Eleme's both-directions branch no longer exists (`0a66800d`), so the fact that put Eleme first is a property of deleted code. And Meituan is worse on both counts — **133 exposed mappings against Eleme's seven**, and nothing downstream that would catch a mislanding, where Eleme now records the listing each push landed on. **THE DISTINCTION BETWEEN THE TWO IS RECORDED ALONGSIDE THE ORDER, BECAUSE WITHOUT IT THE ORDER READS AS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT HAPPENED.** Meituan's exposure is **LATENT**: zero mappings use the loose branch today, every one that resolves resolves exactly, and it fires only on a merchant-side rename or delist — at which point 133 of 393 land on a neighbour. Eleme's was **LIVE**: a fragment resolved and wrote, at least once, and which of three listings took the quantity is still not established. **And Meituan's damage is worse when it fires**, because the truncation collapses families of SIZE VARIANTS onto one key, so a mis-resolve swaps two live stock numbers rather than writing an obviously wrong number onto an unrelated stranger somebody notices. Put plainly: **Eleme has already done harm and can no longer do it that way; Meituan has not yet done harm and would do more of it.** **The rewrite is made in BOTH homes in one pass** — here and `docs/eleme-findings.md` finding 9, which carries this ordering as its own — and marked in place in both, so the two cannot drift apart and a superseded ordering is not met later as a fresh one. Evidence: `docs/meituan-findings.md` findings 1, 4, 5 and 9. A correction to a supporting statement that reverses no rule, hence a patch. Docs only; no code changed.

2026-08-26 · v4.80 — **§30's CHANNEL ORDERING IS CORRECTED: MEITUAN'S EXPOSURE WAS UNDERSTATED, AND THE ORDERING ITSELF IS LEFT STANDING PENDING A DECISION.** v4.79 below describes Meituan as *"substring but one direction only, tempered by an exact-match-first preference and a shortest-name tiebreak"*. **That is accurate about the arm it names and it understates the blast radius by two orders of magnitude, because the damage does not live in that arm.** The containment test does not compare a candidate against our whole name — its middle arm compares the candidate against our name TRUNCATED TO ITS LEADING SAME-SCRIPT RUN, so the rule that reads as "the candidate must contain our name" is in practice "the candidate must contain our name's leading run", which every size variant of one product shares by construction. **Measured: 133 of 393 named mappings would resolve to a NEIGHBOUR if their own listing were renamed or removed — 1 through whole-name containment, the arm v4.79 names, and 132 through the truncation.** They are not strangers: they are coconut yogurt sizes, the nut lines, nut butter jar sizes, chia, kombucha pairs and the foaming hand soap's scents, plus Latin names truncated to stubs that are not words. **A mis-resolve therefore swaps two live stock numbers** — the sibling that took the push, and our own product, which believes it pushed and did not. **The shortest-name tiebreak does not temper this**: it was written to prefer a base product over a 套餐 combo sharing its prefix, and among four pack sizes it picks whichever the merchant named most tersely, which makes the choice deterministic rather than right. **NOTHING DOWNSTREAM CATCHES IT** — the drift sweep compares our record of what we sent against our own shelf count and never reads the channel's stock, so a push that writes the right number to the wrong listing shows no drift and is never re-queued. **THE ORDERING ITSELF IS NOT CHANGED HERE.** Two facts now bear on it — Eleme's both-directions branch was removed on 2026-08-26 and Meituan's exposure is larger than v4.79 implies — but whether Meituan should move is a judgement about intent rather than a fact about the code, and it is left exactly as written until it is ruled on, in this document and in `docs/eleme-findings.md`, so the two cannot drift apart in the meantime. **[ORDERING SUPERSEDED BY v4.81 — rewritten to Meituan first, Eleme second, ordering by standing exposure. Everything else in this entry stands.]** **The correction is marked in place in both**, not folded away.
