A staff-accept step between submit and print is to be supported in the design but left switched off. It is the remedy if phantom orders prove to be a problem in practice.

The QR page is an additional entry point to the same shop listings the till uses. It is not a separate catalogue, a separate order type, or a separate revenue stream.

**Channel and source.** Till sales and QR sales are the same shop selling the same listings and share a single channel value, `shop`. They are never split into separate channels. Order source is recorded separately, distinguishing till from QR, so scan uptake can be measured without dividing a shop's revenue across two channel lines.

This corrects an existing defect rather than inheriting it: counter ledger rows are presently tagged with channel `wechat`, which is a tender name and not a channel. Channel identifies where a sale originated as a business relationship; tender identifies how it was paid. The two are not to be conflated in any new work. Remediation of the existing `wechat`-tagged counter rows is out of scope here and is noted for a separate ruling.

**AMENDED 2026-09-07 by Ash — "order source" above means the column `retail_orders.shop_entry_method`, and its two values are `till` and `qr`. It does NOT mean `retail_orders.source`.** Nothing in the paragraph above is withdrawn or rewritten; the ruling it makes is unchanged and this names the column it left to be inferred.

**The reasoning, recorded because the inference went the other way once already.** `source` answers *how was this row created* — keyed in by staff, or arrived by itself. A till sale and a QR sale are both a person standing in the shop, so `source` cannot separate them: the till's row genuinely was keyed by staff and will go on saying so. `shop_entry_method` was added for exactly this distinction and says so in its own suite — `scripts/test_shop_channel.js` opens by recording that the column exists to say "which of a shop's two doors an order came through — the till or the QR menu (§44)", and that it is "deliberately NOT new values on `source`". **The rule in `routes/retail.js` that a client may not claim `source`** — the comment above the manual-order handler's channel block, stating that `source` "records how the row was CREATED (keyed by staff), which is not something the client gets to claim" — **stands and is correct.** The till keeps posting through that endpoint and that endpoint keeps binding `'manual'`.

**🔴 LIVE DEFECT (RECORDED 2026-09-07, CLOSED THE SAME DAY — see the two paragraphs below): the QR path writes `source = 'qr'` as well as `shop_entry_method = 'qr'`.** The QR submit handler in `routes/shop-menu.js` binds both in one `INSERT` (found today at `:1846`, in `POST /s/:shopCode/order`; a coordinate, per the house rule at the head of this file — find it by the `'shop', 'qr', 'counter'` value row). That widened `source` with a value meaning *which door*, which is the thing its own test file records as deliberately not done. So the two columns disagree about what `source` is for, and the disagreement is in the tree, not in this document.

**Removing it is not a one-liner, which is why it is filed rather than done.** The paid-order auto-print de-dupe reads `prior.source === 'qr'` inside `autoPrintOrder` (found today at `routes/retail.js:27629`) to avoid reprinting a ticket the QR submit already printed. Dropping `source = 'qr'` without moving that predicate onto `shop_entry_method` would reprint every QR order's kitchen ticket on payment. **Whoever fixes this moves the reader and the writer in one commit, or neither.** Historical rows are not in scope: nothing here backfills, and no ruling on backfilling `source` or `channel` is made or implied.

**🔴 CLOSED 2026-09-07, and a WRONG CLAIM IN THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE IS CORRECTED WITH IT.** The defect is fixed: the QR submit handler no longer writes `source` at all, and both readers now key on `shop_entry_method`. **The sentence "It is the only reader of the column anywhere" was FALSE WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN and is struck.** There were TWO readers, and the second was already in the tree at the time — the WeChat payment page in `routes/shop-menu.js`, which 404s an order whose door is not the QR menu (`order.source !== 'qr'`, in the `GET /s/:shopCode/pay/:token` handler). It was missed because the survey behind that sentence searched `routes/retail.js` and stopped at the first hit instead of grepping the pattern across the tree — **exactly the failure this file's own citations rule names: a finding filed as `file:line` is where it was found, not the extent of the problem, and the pattern is grepped before any finding is declared closed.** The correction is recorded rather than the sentence quietly deleted, because the next reader is otherwise free to trust the same method.

**What the fix does, and the one judgement in it.** `source` is now simply absent from the QR `INSERT`, so a QR order stores NULL. **That is not a new value chosen for it; it is what every other self-service path in the system already does** — the mini-app checkout, the web store and the Meituan, Eleme and gzgrocery mirrors all omit the column, and only the staff-keyed manual-order endpoint writes a literal. `source` therefore now reads exactly as this amendment defines it: a value means staff keyed the row, NULL means it arrived by itself. The QR path had been the single self-service writer claiming a value, which is the whole of what was wrong. **Nothing is backfilled**: historical QR rows keep the `source = 'qr'` they were written with, and they remain identifiable by `shop_entry_method`, which those rows also carry.

**Routing.** The menu page is served at `/s/:shopCode`, public, unauthenticated, and outside the admin route tree. `shopCode` is a non-sequential opaque code, not a shop id and not derivable from one. Sequential codes are rejected: a guessable URL would expose other shops' — and in a multi-tenant deployment, other tenants' — menus and pricing to anyone editing the address bar. The code is never typed by a customer; it is only ever scanned.

**Domain.** The page is served from the existing customer-facing domain under the `/s/` path prefix. A new domain is rejected for launch: it would require its own ICP filing before it could be served at all, and a second round of WeChat merchant domain verification when in-page payment is added. A tenant-neutral domain remains open as a later branding decision and is a redirect when it comes.

**Language.** The page opens in the language detected from the client, and inside the WeChat browser that reflects WeChat's own language setting rather than the device OS — a stronger signal of the reader's language than the OS provides. Detection selects the opening language only. A visible language toggle is mandatory, because detection will be wrong for Chinese-speaking guests on English-configured clients and the reverse; the toggle is the correction, not a fallback. This is an exception to §26, permitted because the QR menu is anonymous — there is no reader identity and no stored preference for an inference to override — and §26 continues to govern every identified surface in full.

Consequently every product listed at a shop requires both a Chinese and an English name. This is a launch prerequisite, not a later enhancement. Per §30, Chinese strings are copied from the database or from a locked source, or supplied by Ash — never composed. Products created for a new location have no existing Chinese name and cannot be launched until one is supplied.

## 45. Stock timing for counter and QR orders

Existing behaviour, retained: physical stock is decremented on the paid transition, not at order creation. The reasoning recorded in the code stands — decrementing at creation takes stock for a sale that may never be paid, and the cancel-before-payment path has no reversal hook.

Ruling: a QR order reserves stock on submit and decrements on paid. Reservation and release mechanisms already exist and are used by customer checkout; the counter path has never been wired to them. Reservation prevents the last unit being sold twice during the interval between submit and payment, without moving physical quantity and without requiring a new reversal path.

Cancelling an unpaid order releases the reservation. No physical stock is returned because none was taken.

The sweeps that cancel stale unpaid orders and expire reservations must not apply to counter-fulfilment orders on their existing timings. A customer walking from a table to the till must not have their order cancelled underneath them.

An in-page WeChat payment path is not ruled out and the order lifecycle above is deliberately compatible with it: the cashier's confirmation would be replaced by a payment callback with no other change. It is blocked on a verified 服务号 bound to the existing merchant account — the mini-program appid cannot serve a web page, and no OAuth or JS-SDK code exists in the repo.

## 46. A kitchen sharing a facility with the shelf may correct the count, and a correction is never a batch

Existing behaviour, and it is deliberate rather than an omission: a kitchen operator is never shown a stock quantity. The stock list is rebuilt for them as id, names and SKU only (`routes/retail-inventory.js`, the `kitchenOp` branch in `GET /api/retail-admin/stores/:id/stock`); the stock PATCH refuses anything but a `delta` with `kitchen_add_only`; the Add stock screen hides the All/Low/Out chips, renders `+N` in place of the shelf total, and opens its keypad on the pending amount rather than the count. The recorded reasoning stands and is not overturned: production here is request-driven, the kitchen queue and the "What you made" prefill say what to make, and a shelf number visible to the kitchen invites a tray nobody asked for.

That reasoning assumed the shelf is somewhere the kitchen cannot see. **At Tianhe it is the same facility** — the stock the kitchen adds to is on a shelf the same people can walk to and count.

**Ruling: where the kitchen and the shelf share a facility, the kitchen sees the count and may correct it.** A number they can verify is worth showing; a number they can only look at is not. Showing a total without a way to fix a mismatch is the worse of the two designs — the operator who sees 45 and counts 40 has no honest door, and the dishonest one is open: tapping +5 through the add path to make the number agree. That write is recorded as food that was cooked. §39 ruling 7 already settled the direction of travel for the same shape of problem on a purchase-order receipt: if 8 arrived against 10 on the system, the 10 is the lie and blocking the correction protects it.

**Ruling: adding and correcting are two writes, and the app must never let one become the other.** Adding what was made is a positive delta recorded as production (`kitchen_add`). Correcting the shelf is an absolute count recorded as a recount. They are separate controls, separate entries, separate records. This is the whole reason the ruling above is safe: merged, every yield figure downstream becomes a guess, which is the same failure `made_fewer` exists to prevent in the production gap.

**Ruling (Ash, 2026-09-06): a correction that lowers the count asks why, and the question is a fork rather than a reason picker.** The kitchen records no waste on this screen and the waste vocabulary is deliberately absent from it. The two answers are: the count was wrong, which saves; or something is actually gone, which does not save at all. The second answer routes the loss to whoever holds `waste:record`, and **the count does not move until they record it** — a shelf figure drops because a loss was recorded by someone entitled to record it, never instead of that.

The rejected design is recorded because it is the obvious one and it is wrong under this ruling: offering the waste codes here and writing a waste record from them would put loss-recording in the kitchen's hands through a side door, and offering them without writing a record is worse — a loss named by the operator and filed nowhere.

**Ruling (Ash, 2026-09-06): only a downward correction asks why. A correction that raises the count is saved without a question.** Both readings were put and the friction argument won: raising a count is overwhelmingly a miscount being fixed, and a question asked on every one of them is a question that stops being read. The cost is accepted and named rather than discovered later — an unlogged batch entering through the recount door leaves no reason behind it, and the production record will not show it. What distinguishes it is still the entry itself: a recount is recorded as a recount, never as production, so an increase arriving that way is visibly not a batch even when nobody says why.

**Ruling (Ash, 2026-09-06): the batch screen keeps its full gap vocabulary, waste codes included.** `POST /api/retail-admin/production` is gated on `production:log`, which the kitchen preset holds, and it writes a waste record through `recordProductWaste` when the gap is a loss — so the kitchen already records waste there, and the no-waste rule above does not reach it. The distinction ruled: a gap on a batch the operator has just made, against a request that says how many were expected, is production reporting and is bounded by that batch; opening a fridge and writing off what is in it is not, and is what the rule forbids. Stripping the seven codes there would file two broken jars as "made fewer" and collapse the very distinction `made_fewer` exists to hold open.

**The grant is an existing capability, not a new flag.** `quickstock:recount` (快速库存—盘点(门店)) is already in the registry, already held by the `store_stock` preset, and already accepted by `lib/cap-routes.js` for the stock routes. Granting it to a tenant's kitchen role is the whole mechanism; it is off in the kitchen preset and stays off. **The server must therefore decide by capability and not by job title.** Today `routes/retail-inventory.js` branches on `req.backendUser.role === 'kitchen'`, which is why the behaviour is all-or-nothing. `req.caps` is resolved on every request by `requireRetailAdmin` regardless of `tenants.rbac_enforce`, so reading it does not require a tenant to switch enforcement on.

**The API inconsistency is closed by the same change.** The quantity strip fires today on `req.backendUser.role === 'kitchen'`, but `requireInventoryRead` also admits a plain `users` row carrying `retail_store_id` with no `retail` permission, and such a row whose role is `kitchen` lands in add mode with quantities in the response and only the UI hiding them. Keying the strip on the grant rather than the role covers both realms: an operator in add mode who does not hold the grant is stripped, whichever door they came through.

**NOT DECIDED, and it blocks one control rather than the build:**

- **The Chinese for the fork's two answers.** No live string in the tree fits either. Blocked for Ash per §30; the control ships without them rather than composing them. The waste codes and `made_fewer` keep the Chinese they already carry, and neither appears on this screen.

## 47. A stocked listing with no counted stock at its shop is sold out

A shop listing in stocked mode asserts that the product arrives at that shop as finished goods and that a sale decrements what is on the shelf there. The assertion is about a counted quantity.

Ruling: where a location has never counted units of a listed product — no shelf record for it at all, as distinct from a shelf record reading zero — the menu shows the item as sold out.

The two cases are the same fact. A stocked listing claims the shop holds stock; a shop that has never counted any holds none anyone can vouch for. Absent is not a smaller claim than zero, it is no claim, and a menu is a promise made at a counter.

Rejected: reading an absent shelf record as "not tracked here yet" and showing the item.

**The online store takes the opposite view deliberately, and the two surfaces differ on purpose.** Its catalogue availability — `sellableStockSql` — falls back to a product's flat legacy quantity when the product has no per-location shelf record anywhere, so a newly created product is not born sold out before anyone has stocked it. That is right for a catalogue, which offers to fulfil from wherever stock is, and wrong for a menu, which offers to hand something over at one counter now. Same absent record, two questions, two answers. **Neither is to be changed to match the other.**

Made-here listings are unaffected: they have no shelf record by design and their availability is the manual switch §42 gives them.

This governs the menu only. Nothing here changes the till, the catalogue, an order path, or how stock is counted.

## 48. The standalone stock app is retired, and it is migrated before it is deleted

Ruling (Ash, 2026-09-06): **there is no second app.** `/stock` — the Quick Stock / Add stock PWA — is retired, and every job it holds moves into Tacet Mobile. No stock work runs outside the Tacet system.

**The order is part of the ruling and not a preference: migrate, then delete.** Deleting first is not a faster route to the same place; it strands two roles and six flows that exist nowhere else. What follows is the inventory that makes that concrete, taken from the tree on the day this was decided, so the size of the job is a fact rather than an estimate.

**Already in Tacet, needing nothing:** Receiving (supplier deliveries), Waste, Purchasing, Delivery, Inbox, Sales, Trend, Invoices, New order — and, as of §46's port, Add stock with the count and the correction.

**In `/stock` only, with no home in Tacet at all:** Pick (pulling a run for the stores); Receive delivery — the store end of a transfer, which is a different job from the Receiving row above and must not be folded into it; Ask the kitchen; Ask for stock; Ready from the kitchen; Quick stock, the absolute recount, which is the whole job of the `store_stock` role; and Log a batch / What you made, the production handoff that carries a request's own lines onto the add screen. Kitchen queue and Transfers have rows in Tacet already, but both are departures to `/stock` rather than screens.

**Two roles are LOCKED to the app being deleted.** `kitchen` and `store_stock` carry `stock_app_only`, and `server.js` refuses them Tacet Mobile outright — `/retail-admin` and `/backend/*` redirect them back to `/stock`. Deleting the app before those roles are unlocked leaves both with nothing to open. `lib/stock-app-only.js` and its route allowlist exist only for that confinement and retire with it.

**It is an installed PWA.** `/stock` has its own manifest and icons and sits on staff phones and tablets as an installed shortcut. The retirement leaves `/stock` redirecting into Tacet rather than 404ing, so an installed icon lands somewhere rather than dying; the manifest goes when the redirect has been in place long enough that nobody is opening the shortcut.

**Sequence:**

1. §46's port onto Tacet's Add stock screen — done, and the first step of this rather than a change of direction.
2. Move the homeless flows into Tacet, one at a time, each with its own decision where one is needed: Pick, Receive delivery, Ask the kitchen, Ask for stock, Ready from the kitchen, Quick stock recount, Log a batch. Kitchen queue and Transfers become screens rather than departures in the same pass.
3. Unlock Tacet Mobile for `kitchen` and `store_stock` — drop `stock_app_only` from both presets and retire the gate — once and only once their work exists there.
4. Delete `public/stock.html`, `/stock-login`, the manifest and icons, `lib/stock-app-only.js`, the `/stock` routes and the suites that drive them, leaving the redirect.

**What must not happen at any point:** a role with no app. Step 3 is what makes step 4 safe, and step 2 is what makes step 3 honest.

## 49. The short order code is a plain number that resets each trading day, and an unpaid counter order dies at twenty minutes

§44 rules that a QR order issues "a short order code … what staff use to retrieve the order" and does not say what the code looks like. This section says.

**Ruling (Ash, 2026-09-06): plain numbers, reset daily.** The first order of the trading day is 1, the next is 2, and tomorrow starts again at 1. No prefix, no letter, no shop initial, no date embedded in it.

**Per shop, per trading day.** Two shops both call number 7 on the same afternoon and neither is wrong: the number is spoken across one room and never leaves it. It is not an identifier and must never be used as one — `order_no` remains the order's identity everywhere else in the system, and nothing joins, looks up or reconciles on the short code.

**The day is the trading day, not the calendar day.** It is resolved through `lib/business-date.js` for the order's own location, so a shop trading past midnight keeps one sequence for one night's work rather than restarting mid-service. That also means the reset follows the location's timezone rather than the server's.

**The rejected alternatives are recorded so they are not re-proposed.** A random code cannot be read out — the number is called across a counter and heard over noise, and 4 is heard where A9K3 is not. A code that never resets grows to five digits within a month at one shop. A prefixed code (`R7`, `TH-7`) encodes the shop into something only ever spoken inside that shop, and per §0 a shop initial is tenant data with no business being minted by Tacet.

**Consequence, stated plainly: the code is not unique.** Any screen, report or query that shows a short code shows it with its shop and its date or not at all.

**Ruling (Ash, 2026-09-06): an unpaid counter order is cancelled after twenty minutes, or by staff at any moment, whichever comes first.** §45 exempted counter orders from the stale-order and reservation sweeps and deliberately left their timing open; this closes it. Twenty minutes is long enough to order at a table, wait for it, and queue to pay; short enough that a shop is not holding the last of something for somebody who has left. Staff cancellation is unchanged and immediate — the clock is a floor under it, never a replacement for it.

**It keys on the order's age, not on a reservation.** A made-here order reserves nothing (§43 defers material stock), so a sweep that walks reservations would never see it and such an order would live forever. The clock therefore reads `placed_at` on the order itself.

**Configurable, and switchable off.** `orders.counterAutoCancelMinutes` sets the interval per tenant; `0` turns the clock off entirely and restores staff-only cancellation. Twenty is the default rather than the rule.

*Recorded 2026-09-06, after the code that implements the clock shipped. That is the wrong order and is noted rather than tidied away: the ruling was given, the code was written against it, and the section that should have preceded both is this one.*

## 50. In-page WeChat payment for the QR menu is pursued; Alipay stays a counter payment

§45 left in-page WeChat payment "not ruled out," observing that "the cashier's confirmation would be replaced by a payment callback with no other change," and named what was blocking it: "a verified 服务号 bound to the existing merchant account — the mini-program appid cannot serve a web page, and no OAuth or JS-SDK code exists in the repo."

**Ruling (Ash, 2026-09-06): pursue it.** In his words: *"i want to add payment option with wechat for the qr code menu, and if customer want to pay with alipay they will be directed to the cashier, the receipt will be printed but the payment will be done at the cashier."* The QR menu (`/s/:shopCode`, §44) gains a WeChat payment option that settles the order in-page. A customer who chooses Alipay is routed to the counter instead — the kitchen ticket still prints on submit per §44 either way, but an Alipay order is not treated as paid until staff take the payment there, exactly as every counter order is today. Alipay needs no new architecture: it is the existing cashier-pay path, unchanged.

**The block §45 named is confirmed still standing on a fresh read of the tree, and it is four things, not one.** (1) `tenants.wx_appid` is the only WeChat appid the schema holds anywhere, and it is the Mini Program's; `docs/tacet-pos-counter-survey.md` states directly that "no official-account (服务号) appid is stored anywhere," and what exists is matched against the mini-program payment shape (`wx.requestPayment`), not the JS-SDK shape (`chooseWXPay`) a web page needs. (2) The only openid-producing code in the repo is the mini-program's `wx.login()` → `jscode2session` exchange (`routes/retail.js`), which cannot run outside the mini program; the one other WeChat registration in the codebase, `WECHAT_WEB_APP_ID`/`WECHAT_WEB_APP_SECRET` (`lib/social-auth.js`), is a WeChat Open Platform **website app** used only for desktop scan-to-login (`scope: snsapi_login`) — a third, separate registration, and not payment-capable. (3) No in-browser OAuth code and no JS-SDK code exist anywhere in the repo — a repo-wide search for `wx.config(`, `chooseWXPay`, `jsapi_ticket`, `WeixinJSBridge` and `snsapi_base` found none. (4) §44 already anticipated that in-page payment would need "a second round of WeChat merchant domain verification" for the paying domain, separate from obtaining the account itself; that verification has not been done.

**The first and the fourth are administrative steps with WeChat/Tencent that only the merchant-account holder can complete, and this ruling does not remove them.** Recorded so a later session does not read "Ash decided to pursue in-page WeChat payment" as "the credentials exist" — they do not yet, and no code change in this repo can substitute for the registration or the domain verification.

**Sequencing, so the build is not left waiting on paperwork it does not yet need:** the OAuth handshake and the JS-SDK payment trigger can be designed and written against WeChat's published contract without live credentials, the same way `lib/tenant-creds.js` already holds every other WeChat Pay secret per tenant rather than in one global config — a `wechat.official_account` credential group is the natural home once the account exists. What cannot happen without the real 服务号 and its domain verification is turning it on: there is no sandbox standing in for a verified official account on this integration, so the first true end-to-end test is necessarily against production credentials.

**Ruling (Ash, 2026-09-06): the kitchen ticket's trigger follows the payment path, and §44 is NARROWED rather than overturned.** §44 rules that the ticket prints on submit, which was right while every QR order was paid at a counter with staff watching the customer. An in-page WeChat order is not that: the customer can submit, close WeChat and never pay, and the food is already made. **A QR order taking the in-page WeChat path therefore prints on payment success; every other QR order keeps §44's print-on-submit** — Alipay, cash, and anyone routed to the counter. The cost is named rather than discovered: a few seconds between the customer's confirmation and the ticket, bought against never printing a ticket for food nobody paid for. §44's rule is not deleted and governs the counter-paid path unchanged.

**Consequence for §49's clock, stated so it is not rediscovered:** an unpaid in-page order that dies at twenty minutes now leaves no printed ticket behind it, which is the waste this ruling exists to prevent. The clock itself is unchanged.

> **SUPERSEDED IN PART, 2026-09-08 (v4.150) — decided by Ash.** The sentence above that "every other QR order keeps §44's print-on-submit — Alipay, cash, and anyone routed to the counter" no longer holds: **every QR order now prints on paid, and none prints on submit.** This ruling's *reasoning* is not superseded, it is generalised — what changed is that its premise, "paid at a counter with staff watching the customer", stopped being the whole story. The counter can now see a QR order before the customer reaches it, in the till's own pending list, so the ticket no longer has to run ahead of them to reach the kitchen. The cost this ruling named is now paid on every order and is named again in the v4.150 entry. The half of this section that survives unchanged is the mechanism: `autoPrintOrder`'s skip guard is `shop_entry_method='qr' AND print_status='printed'`, an order that never printed reaches the paid transition with `print_status` null, and the guard does not fire — which is why generalising the rule needed no change inside `autoPrintOrder` either time.

**Ruling (Ash, 2026-09-06): there is no in-page payment fallback outside the WeChat browser, and those customers pay at the counter.** A customer who opens the menu with a phone camera rather than WeChat's own scanner lands in Safari or Chrome, where WeChat's in-page payment cannot run at all. That customer is routed to the counter and pays there, **where staff scan the customer's payment code on the existing terminal** — the flow the shop already runs, and no new code. **Rejected: rendering a WeChat Pay Native QR on the page for them.** It is buildable today and is rejected for the same reason as the interim below: a second QR scanned out of a camera app is a worse counter than the counter.

**The payment page DOES read the user agent, and §47's rule that nothing on the menu branches on it is untouched.** The two look like a contradiction and are not. §47's property — held by a test that fetches `/s/:shopCode` under three user agents and compares the bytes — is that *what a shop sells* never depends on what someone reads it with. The payment page asks a different question, on a different route: WeChat's in-page sheet physically cannot run outside WeChat, so a customer who is outside it must be sent to the counter per the ruling above. **The alternative is worse than knowing.** Sending that customer to WeChat's authorize URL anyway strands them on WeChat's own error page — the one outcome this page must never produce — because the redirect leaves our server and never comes back. The check governs only which of two screens is shown; no price, no availability and nothing about the order moves on it, and the menu's byte-identical test still runs with the rail switched on.

**Rejected for now: shipping WeChat Pay Native (a second scannable QR code) as an interim in-page option.** It needs no new registration, and existing code already knows how to generate one (`wechatNativePrepare`, `routes/retail.js`) — but it was not what was asked for, since a customer would still leave the one-tap flow to scan a second code with their camera, and Ash chose the real in-page (JSAPI) path over shipping that as a stopgap.

**NOT DECIDED:**

- The Chinese copy for the "pay with Alipay at the counter" message on the QR menu. No live string in the tree fits it; per the Chinese-strings delegation this is composed and declared in `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` in the same commit as the code that uses it, not a reason to block the build.
- The exact fields the future `wechat.official_account` credential group needs, and whatever JS-SDK ticket caching it settles on — deferred to the session that writes that code, once the account exists.
- Whether the order model needs a new payment-pending sub-state to distinguish "waiting on a WeChat callback" from today's `pending_payment`, or whether the existing counter-order status machine (§45, §49) already covers it — deferred to that same session.

Docs only; no code yet.

## 51. A kitchen request prints on paper when it reaches the queue; one kitchen printer, and the tenant says when it prints

A warehouse→kitchen request has announced itself since #261: it fans out by
capability to every operator holding `restock:fulfil` and opens on
`/stock?go=queue`. That reaches a phone. **A kitchen is a room with wet hands,
noise and no phone on the bench**, and Ash raised it as exactly that: *"when
there is a request from the kitchen and it arrive to the kitchen queue — except
of notification, i want to have a printer that printer the order for them in the
kitchen."*

**Ruling (Ash, 2026-09-06): build it.** A request landing in the production
queue also comes out of a thermal printer in the kitchen. The notification is
not replaced — paper is an addition, and the push still goes out unchanged.

**NOTHING NEW IS WIRED FOR IT, and that is most of why this was a day's work
rather than a project.** The store printers already run on Feieyun's cloud
(`lib/feie.js`): the server POSTs the slip text to the Open API and the cloud
pushes it to the device, which prints and announces by voice within a second or
two. No LAN, no agent, no port forwarding — which is why a remote server
printing to an on-site printer works at all. **The kitchen's printer is one more
device on the SAME Feieyun account**, so this is a second caller of an existing
rail rather than a second rail. The pattern it copies wholesale is the paid-order
auto-print: best-effort, fire-and-forget, and recording BOTH outcomes.

**Ruling (Ash, 2026-09-06): one kitchen printer, not a map keyed by location.**
The alternative was offered and declined: the store printers resolve through
`printer.by_store`, keyed on store id, and a per-location kitchen map would have
made a second kitchen a config row rather than a code change. Ash chose the
single printer. **The reasoning is recorded because the cost is real and lands
later**: a second kitchen means changing the config shape, migrating the saved
value, and touching the routing again. It is a new decision when it happens,
not a row nobody would have filled in.

**The single SN is also what the data model already forces**, which is worth
recording beside the ruling because it means the two answers do not conflict
today. A kitchen request carries **no locations at all** — `routes/restock.js`
nulls both `from_store_id` and `to_store_id` for any order with a kitchen at
either end, because a kitchen request is production and not a transfer between
shelves (§43's distinction, applied). So there is nothing for a store map to key
on, and `printer.kitchen_sn` is a standalone setting rather than a `by_store`
row.

**Ruling (Ash, 2026-09-06): WHEN it prints is a per-tenant setting, and Roots
prints on arrival only.** In his words: *"It depends on the tenant. For roots
only when job arrive."* So `printer.kitchen_print_on` takes `sent` (the
default, and Roots' answer), `prepared`, `both`, or `off`. **The reason arrival
alone is right for Roots is worth stating**: the people who would read a
completion slip are the people who just cooked it, and the person actually
waiting to hear that the food is made is at the other end of a push, not in the
kitchen. A tenant that wants a spike of finished tickets can have one; Roots
does not.

**`delivered` never prints, in any setting.** A warehouse→kitchen request closes
at `prepared` — §39's shape, already encoded in `PUSH_AUDIENCE`, which gives the
kitchen direction no `delivered` entry at all.

**A transfer between shelves NEVER reaches the kitchen's roll**, and this is
held by a test rather than by the absence of a call site. A kitchen printing
every store's restock is a kitchen that stops reading the printer.

**THE SLIP CARRIES NO MONEY.** Not the unit cost, not a line total, not a
total — a production ticket is not priced, and a cost column on one would only
invite the kitchen to think a transfer owes it something. It carries the request
number, why it was asked for (§39's `purpose`, `order` or `shelf`), who asked
and when, every line with its quantity and unit, and the requester's note.

**A FAILED PRINT IS RECORDED, NOT SWALLOWED, and that is not optional here.**
`restock_orders` gains `print_status` / `printed_at` / `print_error` — the same
three `retail_orders` already carries — because the one certainty about a
thermal printer in a kitchen is that some morning it is out of paper. The queue
screen shows the failure and offers a reprint. **A result that never reached a
printer is NOT a failure**: no SN configured, the event switched off, or an
order that was never a kitchen request are all "no slip was owed", and recording
one as failed would put a red mark and a reprint button on a request that was
never printing.

**Two defects were found by the suite written for this and are fixed in the same
commit.** They are recorded because both are the kind that would have shipped
green. (1) `kitchenScopedOrder` — the middleware that refuses a store transfer
on every kitchen endpoint — **only guards a KITCHEN-realm session and returns
early for a Tacet operator**, who since #261 is exactly who works this queue.
The reprint's refusal was leaning on it and therefore was not refusing. The
guard now sits on the endpoint. **The middleware itself is NOT changed here**:
whether its realm check is right for the endpoints that have relied on it since
#261 is a larger question than this build, and is left open below rather than
answered in passing. (2) The reprint stamped its outcome unconditionally, so
refusing a transfer stamped `print_status = 'failed'` on the transfer.

**NOT DECIDED:**

- ~~Whether `kitchenScopedOrder`'s realm-scoped guard is right for the other
  endpoints that use it.~~ **AUDITED THE SAME DAY AND WITHDRAWN — the concern
  as filed was wrong, and it is corrected here rather than left for someone to
  spend a day on.** The claim was that the guard is "a no-op for a Tacet
  session", which is false. `_kitchenScopedSession` is true for a kitchen-realm
  session OR for an operator holding `restock:fulfil` and NOT `restock:pick`,
  and computing that across every shipped preset gives exactly one match: the
  `kitchen` role. Every other role that can reach these endpoints — `owner`,
  `admin`, `manager`, `warehouse`, `store_manager` — holds `restock:pick` or no
  restock capability at all, and each of them works transfers legitimately, so
  passing through is the correct behaviour rather than an opening. **The guard
  is a SCOPE limiter keyed on a role shape ("a kitchen account may only touch
  kitchen requests"), and it does that job.** What the reprint endpoint needed
  was a different thing — an OBJECT-TYPE guard, "this endpoint only ever
  operates on a kitchen request, for anybody" — which is why the fix was to put
  the check on the endpoint and is why the middleware is correctly left alone.
  **Two observations recorded from the audit, neither a defect:** the endpoints
  are capability-gated by `lib/cap-routes.js` (`/api/restock` is covered) only
  once a tenant switches on `tenants.rbac_enforce`, which is the documented
  Phase 2 position and not a finding; and `resolveOperator` fails OPEN by
  design, so a capability-resolution error leaves a kitchen operator unscoped
  rather than locked out — consistent with that module's stated contract.
- **A second kitchen.** Ruled above as a single printer; when a second kitchen
  exists, the config shape is a new decision.
- **Whether the kitchen realm's own screen (`public/kitchen.html`) gains the
  reprint control.** It is still a client of these endpoints and its request
  detail view is the obvious second home for the button. Left out of this build
  to keep one PR to one change; the endpoint serves both realms already.

## 52. A mirrored order has no parcels

An order mirrored in from someone else's system — Meituan, Eleme, gzgrocery —
is a **ledger row**, not work. We do not accept it, prepare it, pack it, put it
on a courier or enter a waybill for it; the platform that owns it does all of
that. Ash raised the gap from a phone, looking at gzgrocery order GZ-140695:
*"no way I'll for gzgrocery. this is mobile. no land it air option."*

**Ruling (Ash, 2026-09-06): a mirrored order gets no shipment rows, ever, and
no screen offers a parcel mode or a waybill for one.**

### The card was not a display bug — we were creating the parcel

Four steps, each correct on its own:

1. `scripts/gzgrocery-order-daemon.js` mirrors the order in with
   `fulfillment_type = 'delivery'` and no address. That is the honest value —
   the goods did go somewhere — and there is no fourth fulfilment type meaning
   "not ours to fulfil".
2. The order-detail read calls `shipsNothing(o) ? [] : ensureShipments(id)`.
   `shipsNothing` (`lib/fulfilment.js`) answers pickup and counter. **It has
   never read a channel**, so a mirrored order is planned like any delivery.
3. `planShipments` finds an empty destination city: not Guangzhou, not
   Guangdong, so it falls through to the air/land split. **It lands on Land
   for a second reason worth recording, because it is one column from being
   worse**: the mirror does not copy `ship_modes` either, so
   `COALESCE(ship_modes, 'air,land')` gives every mirrored line the Any bucket,
   which `bucketForItem` sends to land. **Cold chain is NOT a factor** — it
   stopped being a per-item one when ice packing moved to "everything in the
   air parcel is packed with ice anyway". So the Air parcel is reachable only
   for an air-ONLY product, which is a mode the mirror has no way to set today
   and would set the moment anyone taught it to copy the column.
4. The order's status is `delivered`, so the legacy back-fill stamps that
   phantom parcel dispatched and delivered — which is exactly what promotes it
   into the phone's hoisted tracking block.

The result on the glass: **"Land — No waybill on this parcel yet — add it on
the desktop."**

### And the instruction could not be followed

The desktop routes a read-only channel to `renderReadonlyOrder`, which renders
no parcels, no tracking and no waybill field. So the phone was sending an
operator to a screen that does not offer the thing it named. **The desktop was
never right about this, only silent** — it hid the rows its own drawer opens
were causing to be written.

### Both ends, and the reason is asymmetric

**Ruling: the server stops planning them AND the phone stops showing them.**
Not belt-and-braces — each half covers what the other cannot:

- Stopping the planner alone leaves every mirrored order **already opened once**
  carrying its Land row. There is no self-heal: the detail read returns `[]`
  for these orders rather than reconciling them.
- Guarding the phone alone leaves the rows accumulating on every drawer open,
  for every other reader.

Existing phantom rows are **left in place, not swept**. Nothing reads them once
both guards are in, a delete migration over live order data is a larger
decision than this one, and a row that is never read is cheaper than a
migration that is wrong.

### The rule is the channel set, not gzgrocery

**Ruling: Meituan, Eleme and gzgrocery.** Meituan
(`routes/meituan-internal.js`) and Eleme (`routes/eleme-internal.js`) mirror in
with the same `fulfillment_type='delivery'` and grow the same phantom parcels;
gzgrocery is simply the one with a phone screen pointed at it. The set is the
one the desktop's `ordIsReadonlyChannel` has used since these channels landed —
`isMirroredChannel` in `lib/fulfilment.js` is that list given a name the server
can share.

### The guard goes inside ensureShipments, against this repo's own convention

Fulfilment type is guarded at each of the eleven callers, and `ensureShipments`
deliberately reads no fulfilment column. **The channel guard is put inside it
anyway**, and the precedent for doing so is in this file's own §24 record: the
split/undo branch was the one caller that forgot, created Air/Land parcels for
a counter sale, and the damage persisted because the detail read returns `[]`
for those orders instead of reconciling them.

**A channel that ships nothing of ours is a property of the ORDER, not of one
read path.** Enforced at the single materialisation point, it cannot be
forgotten by caller twelve. The endpoints that ask for parcels on a mirrored
order now get an empty list and refuse, which is the correct answer.

### shipsNothing is deliberately NOT widened

It would have been one line, and it would have broken a live rail.
`maybeEnqueueQingyunPush` gates on `shipsNothing`, and **a Meituan order really
is fulfilled by a Qingyun rider** — the desktop's read-only drawer shows that
rider card and its dispatch control on purpose. Widening `shipsNothing` to
cover mirrored channels would stop the rider push on the channel that most
needs it. Two different questions — "does a parcel of ours leave?" and "is this
order ours to fulfil at all?" — get two predicates.

### Mobile gains the channel set the desktop already had

The phone computed `viewOnly` from its display-channel key, which has **no
Eleme entry at all** — so an Eleme order was not read-only on the phone in any
respect. It now reads the raw channel through the same helper, which also
corrects the list row's delivery cell.

### NOT decided / not fixed here

- **The ship-by tile still reads "Ship when ready · courier" on a mirrored
  order.** Same class of fiction as the Land card, different tile, and
  `annotateShipBy` guards `shipsNothing` only. One PR to one change; this is
  the next one.
- **The waybill POST answers `no_shipments` with a 500.** Correct refusal,
  wrong code — a mirrored order asking for a waybill is a 4xx. Untouched
  because no shipped screen offers it.
- **Mobile's `CH_ICON` / `CH_BACK` have no Eleme entry**, so an Eleme order
  wears the mini-app icon and lands in the mini-app channel filter. Display
  only, and a separate change.
- **The phone's DRAWER carries no read-only marking at all.** Found while
  writing the probe for this change, which had assumed one: the "View only"
  pill is the LIST row's, and the sheet says nothing — where the desktop's
  read-only panel tags its own header with the channel and "view only". So an
  operator who opens a mirrored order from the list loses the only thing on
  screen telling them it is not theirs to work. The probe asserts the mapped
  `viewOnly` flag instead of a pill, and this is left as its own change rather
  than added in passing.
- **The phantom rows already written are not swept.** See above.

## 53. The Quick Stock and Add Stock feature switches are deleted ahead of §48's last step

**WRITTEN AS §52 AND RENUMBERED TO §53 ON REBASE, 2026-09-06.** PR #335 merged
its own §52 — a mirrored order has no parcels — while this was being written on
an open branch, so that one keeps the number and this takes the next. **Nothing
was renumbered to make room and no live section moved**, which is the whole of
the append-only rule at the head of this file. This is the third collision of
its kind recorded here, after two branches each defining a §39 and the §46/§47
pair, and it arose the same way each time: two branches open at once, each
taking what was the next free number when it was written. **Version becomes
v4.138**; v4.137 is #335's and is not touched.

**DECIDED 2026-09-06 by Ash.** The two Features switches — `quickStock` ("Quick
Stock (mobile)" · 手机库存) and `kitchenAdd` ("Add Stock (kitchen)" · 加库存) —
are removed from both Settings screens now, rather than retiring with `/stock`
in §48 step 4. Ash's framing: Quick Stock became part of Tacet and is no longer
connected to the kitchen app, so the switches no longer describe anything an
operator recognises.

**THE SWITCHES WERE ALREADY HALF-DEAD, AND THAT IS THE FINDING THAT PROMPTED
THIS.** Both are operator preferences in `storefront_config`
(`features.quickStock`, `features.kitchenAdd`). They are NOT members of
`lib/features.js` `FEATURES`, so they never had an entitlement layer, and the
`feature:` tags carried by `quickstock:add` and `quickstock:recount` in
`lib/capabilities.js` were therefore inert: `entitlements()` only ever emits
keys drawn from `FEATURES`, so `backend-team.js`'s
`ent[c.feature] === false` filter could not fire for either. The only server
reader was a pair of private helpers in `routes/retail-inventory.js`, folded
into one `enabled` field on `/api/retail-admin/quick-stock/context`, and the
only consumer of that field was the standalone `/stock` PWA's "off" screen.

**Tacet Mobile's own Add stock / Quick stock screens never read it.** They call
the same endpoint and take `can_recount` and `stores` from the response while
ignoring `enabled`; entry to those screens is gated on capability alone. So the
switch an operator was holding in Tacet's own Settings changed nothing in
Tacet. **`kitchenAdd`'s own copy — "Off: kitchen staff cannot add what they
just made" — was false at the time of this ruling**, because they could, from
More → Add stock. `quickStock`'s copy named `/stock` explicitly and was
literally true, but sat in a list where every other row governs the app the
reader is holding.

**THE COST IS RECORDED RATHER THAN GLOSSED.** `/stock` is still live under
§48 — still served, still the only home for six flows, and `kitchen` and
`store_stock` still carry `stock_app_only` — so deleting the switches takes
away that app's only off switch while two roles remain locked inside it. That
is accepted, not overlooked: the switch was a kill switch nobody could reach a
correct conclusion from, and §48 deletes the app it guarded regardless. **§48's
ordering rule is otherwise untouched** — migrate before delete still governs
the app itself, and nothing here unlocks a role or removes a flow.

**A tenant currently holding either preference at `false` has that app switched
back on by this change.** A migration deletes both `storefront_config` rows so
the stored `false` cannot sit in the database meaning nothing; leaving it would
be indistinguishable to a later reader from a preference still honoured.

**The context endpoint keeps sending `enabled: true` as a constant.** `/stock`
is an installed PWA. Its shell is network-first and not precached, so a stale
copy is bounded — but a cached `stock.html` that still tested the field would
read an omitted `enabled` as falsy and show every staffer the "off" screen. The
constant costs one line and removes that failure mode entirely; it goes when
the app does.

**Rejected, both offered and declined:** narrowing the two labels to say they
govern the separate `/stock` app and deleting them with the app in §48 step 4;
and wiring the flags into Tacet Mobile so the switches became true rather than
removed — investment in a control §48 already retires.

Code, docs, schema and one migration. No change to any capability grant, and no
role gains or loses access to either screen.

## 54. The phone's order drawer reads the fields it already holds on a mirrored order

**DECIDED by Ash, 2026-09-07**, from a phone, looking at GZ-140695: *"on PC you
can find address and name. can gather all info that PC version have for
gzgrocery order and add them to mobile"*.

§52 settled what the drawer must **not** show on a mirrored order — no parcel,
no waybill, no shipping mode. This is the other half: what it must show.

### The finding

**Both surfaces read the same payload.** `GET /api/retail-admin/orders/:id` is
`SELECT o.*` joined to the customer and store, so `recipient_name`,
`recipient_phone`, `address_full` and the `address` parsed out of
`address_json` all reach the phone already. Nothing here was a missing field, a
missing column or a missing endpoint. **Every gap was the phone declining to
render something it was holding**, which is why this is a client change with no
route, schema or capability touched.

### The load-bearing one: the customer blob

gzgrocery mirrors OpenCart's whole customer cell — `"Name (phone) address…"` —
into `recipient_name`, and its `recipient_phone` and ship columns stay null.
The desktop has split that back into a name and a phone since the column
existed (`ordCustomerLines`, `public/retail-admin/04-orders.js`); the phone
printed it raw, so **the address landed in the name line** and the card read as
one long run-on where the desktop shows two clean fields.

Ported verbatim — same channel test, same `\((\d{6,})\)` pattern, same
six-digit floor — rather than reimplemented, **so the two surfaces cannot
disagree about who an order is for**. Every other channel writes real columns
and passes straight through, and a gzgrocery order that *has* a real phone
column is not split either: this is a repair for a missing column, not a parser
we run on every row.

**A placeholder row is left exactly as it is.** An order whose dispatch note was
never read carries the order id echoed into `recipient_name`
(`scripts/gzgrocery-order-daemon.js`, "Prefer the real recipient"). There is no
blob to split there, and nothing in this change invents a name or an address the
row does not hold — **which is what GZ-140695 itself still does after it**, and
what the desktop does with the same row.

### The five others, each a field already in hand

- **When the order was placed.** `orderHeadMarks` has guarded on `placedFull`
  since it was written — its own comment opens "when the order was placed" — and
  nothing ever set it, so the strip drew only on the marks and the drawer
  carried no date at all. On a mirrored order, with nothing to pack and nothing
  to dispatch, when it was placed is most of what there is to read. Carried raw
  and formatted at render time, never at map time: `state.liveDetail` is cached
  and the language toggle only re-renders.
- **The read-only tag.** The desktop tags its mirrored panel; the phone's
  "View only" pill was the **list row's**, so opening the order lost the one
  fact explaining why nothing in it can be acted on.
- **The variant.** `ITEM_TUPLE` read `options` and never `size`. A storefront
  line carries the customer's own choices in `options`; a mirrored one has none
  and puts its variant in `size`, which is what the desktop's read-only manifest
  prints as the line's type. Added as a fallback, so a storefront line's own
  options still win.
- **The money-gap band.** The drawer showed a total, showed the lines, and said
  nothing when the two contradicted each other — and on a mirrored order the
  phone is often the only place anyone looks. Ported with the desktop's
  tolerance (¥5 or 30%) and its inclusive/exclusive tax rule.
- **The SKU chip.** Inert, where the desktop links the line out to its product.
  It now opens the phone's own product sheet, and only when the lookup behind it
  can succeed.

### Rulings

- **The read-only tag rides the marks strip, not the header.** The header is
  order number, status pill and close button on a 390px screen; a fourth item
  there squeezes the order number into an ellipsis. The strip is full-width and
  wraps.
- **It reads the RAW channel, not the display key.** `CH_BACK` still has no
  Eleme entry (§52), so an Eleme order read through the display key would be
  tagged "mini-app". Platform names are brands — the same word in both
  languages — so they are a data map and never `T()` pairs, which is the shape
  `test_mobile_screens`' bilingual check exists to reject.

### A defect found in the same card and fixed with it

The Ship-to **Copy** button spread a null address (`T(...o.addr)`), so on every
order with none on file — a counter sale, a pickup, and every gzgrocery mirror —
the one button on that card threw a `TypeError` and copied nothing at all. It
now joins the parts that exist, the way the desktop's copy chip does, and drops
a `—` rather than pasting a placeholder into a shipping label.

### Deliberately not done

- **The ship-by tile still says "Ship when ready · courier" on a mirrored
  order.** It is visible in the screenshot that prompted this change, and §52
  already recorded it as a separate change — so it stays one rather than being
  folded in here.
- **Three of the desktop's mirrored cards were examined and not ported**,
  because none can fire on this channel: `renderChannelMoneyPanel` returns early
  for anything but Meituan and Eleme, and the gzgrocery daemon writes neither
  `channel_status` nor `channel_eta` nor `needs_cutlery`. Porting them would
  have added three cards that are dead by construction.

### Strings

**None composed.** Every pair is either already live in `m.html` ("View only")
or lifted from `04-orders.js` ("Order placed · 下单于", "Total disagrees with the
items · 金额与商品不符", and the two sentences of the gap band), so
`docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` is untouched.

### Scope

Client and docs. `public/m.html`, one new suite
(`scripts/test_mobile_mirrored_order_info.js`, 37 assertions across 16 cases)
registered in the slow shard beside the §52 suite, and this entry. No route,
schema, migration or capability change.

## 55. Revenue is orders, and only orders

Decided by Ash, 2026-09-07.

Finance revenue counts orders across every channel — manual orders, Meituan, Eleme, mini app, till counter, and any channel a tenant adds later. It is one row per order.

Hand-typed `income_entries` rows are NOT revenue. They are money in, and they belong on their own staircase row below the revenue line, feeding Net. A tenant typing in an equipment sale or a refunded deposit has not made a sale, and folding it into revenue would corrupt every channel comparison and every AI sentence drawn from it.

THE DEFECT THIS FIXES: Summary reported money-in from `retail_orders` while Transactions reported it from `income_entries`, one tab apart, never reconciling. Whichever a chart or an AI read had picked up would have been arbitrary.

OPEN, AND IT MUST BE SETTLED BEFORE ANY FINANCE CHART SHIPS: the Tacet Summary counts `retail_orders`. The kitchen POS writes `sales_entries`, a different table. If till-counter takings land in `sales_entries` and not in `retail_orders`, Tacet's revenue figure is short by that amount today and no screen says so. This is a survey question, not an assumption.

## 56. Cost of goods and gross profit stay blank

Decided by Ash, 2026-09-07.

`cost_of_goods` and `gross_profit` remain null on the Finance summary. Both rows render blank. Net is revenue minus operating expenses, and is therefore structurally higher than true net — this is known and accepted, not a defect to be quietly patched.

REJECTED: deriving cost of goods from ingredient purchases falling inside the window. Purchases are lumpy and sales are not. A ¥2,000 delivery on the 3rd would crater the margin for one window and inflate the next with no change in the business, and an AI reading it would report a delivery date as a trend.

This follows the standing rule that a product with an incomplete cost shows blank, never a silently low number. A wrong margin at the top of the finance screen is worse than a blank one, because a tenant will price from it.

True cost at the moment of sale is §31 and remains parked. When §31 lands, these two rows fill from it and nothing else.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE AI: the finance read is forbidden from discussing margin, gross profit, or cost of goods in any form, including inference from other figures. This is a hard constraint in its prompt, not a preference.

## 57. Finance charts are hand-rolled SVG, shared with Reports

Decided by Ash, 2026-09-07.

No charting library is introduced. Finance charts are hand-written SVG, as Reports already does at `public/retail-admin/03-dashboard.js:3286`.

The chart primitives are extracted into a shared module BEFORE Finance draws anything, and Finance and Reports both consume it. Two hand-rolled copies of the same chart is the "shared components live in one place and are never re-implemented per page" rule broken, and it drifts silently — a change made for one page leaves the other on the old look with nobody noticing.

Charts obey the existing rules: no gridlines, no axis box, no gradient, one accent colour and only where it means something, one question per chart.

## §58 — A FRESH LINE ON AN ORDER THAT IS NOT GOING OUT TODAY IS DEDUCTED WHEN IT GOES OUT, NOT WHEN IT IS PAID

Decided by Ash, 2026-09-07, from an order screenshot: *"这是包含鲜食的预约单，明天发送。但是鲜食的库存已经自动扣除了。if that's correct then it's not following the rule we agreed on"* — TC000578, eight lines, eleven units, 空运 to 北京, paid and unshipped, its 鲜食 already off the count.

### The ruling

A **batch-made** line — `store_products.is_batch_made = 1`, the kitchen's own flag, the same one the fresh pre-order exemption reads — on an order that is **not handed over at the counter** does NOT decrement `physical_qty` at the paid transition. It decrements at the first forward transition into fulfilment, where the existing calls already take it: Start preparing, Mark dispatched, a parcel dispatched, a waybill pasted, a JD waybill minted, a rider collecting.

**Every other line on the same order still decrements at payment**, including every grocery line in the same basket. The 2026-08-31 change — *every paid order decrements, whatever its address* — **stands for everything that is not made in the kitchen**, and is not reopened here.

**A counter sale is excluded by name.** It is handed over in the same instant it is paid; the food has already left the fridge. `isCounter` is the test, not the absence of an address.

### Why the fresh line is different, and a jar is not

The shop sells a sold-out fresh item on a stated premise: the kitchen makes the next batch on a named day, and the delivery date is floored onto that day. That premise is enforced in code — the fresh exemption in the local pre-order gate turns the refusal off only for a caller that floors the date, and the order carries `promised_ship_date` / `promised_delivery_date`, which the kitchen slip prints as *MAKE FRESH 当天现做*.

**Deducting at payment contradicts that premise twice.** It takes tomorrow's food out of today's count, so today's shoppers are told sold out while the units sit in the fridge; and where the shelf is already at zero — which the fresh exemption deliberately permits — it drives `physical_qty` negative, because that decrement path performs no availability check at all.

A shelf-stable jar has no batch behind it. If its count does not move at payment, the out-of-stock gate reads the same number for the next shopper and the next, and the shop oversells stock it does not have with nothing to make good on it. That is exactly what the 2026-08-31 change was made to stop, and it is why this ruling is narrow: **the kitchen's cadence is what earns the deferral, so only what the kitchen makes gets it.**

### What is NOT changed

- **Guangzhou same-day is untouched.** Those orders reserve at checkout and commit their reservations on payment. Nothing on this path reaches them, and their food does leave today.
- **No new decrement site, no new ledger reason.** The deferred line lands on the existing `order_prepare` row written by the existing fulfilment-transition calls. The per-product idempotency guard already skips a product that reserved or already decremented, so a mixed order commits its grocery half at payment and its fresh half later, with neither double-counting.
- **Refunds need no change and get none.** The ledger-backed reverser caps each product at what the ledger says is still out, so a deferred line that was never decremented returns nothing. This is arithmetic, not a new flag.
- **No new strings.** The operator already has the *Stock pending · 库存待扣* note and its title *Real stock deducts once this order moves to Preparing · 库存要等这单推进到备货中才会真正扣减*, which is once again true of exactly these orders. `docs/tacet-delivery-vocabulary.md` is untouched.
- **No schema change and no migration.** Both flags this reads already exist.

### One gap this opened, and closed with it

**The two auto-deliver sweeps can claim an order straight out of `paid`** — `AUTO_DELIVER_FROM_STATUSES` is `['paid','preparing','dispatched','rider_pickup']` — and neither committed stock, because until now nothing was ever owed by the time they ran: payment had already taken it. **With the kitchen's lines held back, a sweep closing a local fresh pre-order would have stranded those units on the count with nothing left to fire.** Both sweeps therefore gained the same idempotent call every other forward transition makes, labelled *Auto · delivered (ETA)* and *Auto · delivered (rider)*. It is a no-op for the preparing and dispatched orders they mostly close.

**This is the shape to look for if the deferral is ever widened:** the held-back line is only safe while every path out of `paid` takes it, and that set is not obvious from the status column alone.

### Recorded, and deliberately NOT fixed here

1. **NOTHING CAPS HOW MANY PRE-ORDERS ONE BATCH TAKES.** The fresh exemption admits a sold-out batch-made line without comparing the quantity asked for against the batch that will cover it. Forty orders against a batch of twenty are accepted today and would be accepted after this change; what moves is only that the count no longer drifts downward while it happens. **A batch-capacity gate is separate work and is not implied by this ruling** — it needs a batch size per product per day, which §40 defines for a recipe and nothing yet exposes to checkout.
2. **THE STOCK-PENDING NOTE IS ORDER-ITEM DEEP, NOT BUNDLE DEEP.** The badge asks whether the order holds a batch-made item still owed; a bundle whose *components* are batch-made is not walked, because the badge is an operator hint and walking bundles per list row is a query per row. The decrement itself is unaffected — it runs on the expanded component lines and always did.
3. **`is_batch_made`, NOT `oos_policy = 'backorder_gz'`.** The broader policy flag lets an operator open any product to out-of-city pre-order, kitchen-made or not, and a shelf item opened that way still has no batch behind it. The narrow flag is the one that means *the kitchen makes this*, and it is the one the rest of the fresh machinery already reads.


## §59 — THE KITCHEN QUEUE HANDS OVER ON THE CAPABILITY THAT SCREEN'S WRITE IS GATED ON, NOT ON THE QUICK-STOCK MODE

Decided by Ash, 2026-09-07, from the report that *"the kitchen queue, after making the next window should be how many items reached the shelf but that window never open"*.

### What was wrong

"What you made" is the screen between closing a kitchen request and the shelf being right. Marking a request `prepared` moves no stock — that is §39 and is correct — so the queue is supposed to carry the request's own lines straight onto the screen that adds them. The queue says so on the button's own screen: *The next screen asks how many reached the shelf.*

It never did. `hdStart` in `public/m.html` opened only when `qsMode()==='add'`. That mode comes off `/api/retail-admin/quick-stock/context`, and `lib/quick-stock-grant.js` derives it from the **role**, not from a capability: `'add'` is returned only for a backend operator whose `tenant_users.role` is literally `kitchen`. That role ships `stock_app_only`, and `server.js` uses that flag to keep it out of Tacet Mobile entirely — a page request to `/retail-admin` is redirected to `/stock`, and every `/api/` call outside `lib/stock-app-only.js`'s allowlist is refused `kitchen_add_only`.

**The two conditions could therefore never both hold.** Everybody who can open this queue reads `'recount'`. `hdStart` returned false on every tap, `kqAdvance` fell through to the queue, and the promise made one screen earlier was kept for nobody.

### The ruling

**The handover is gated on `production:log`, asked through `canRoute('whatmade')`** — the capability `POST /api/retail-admin/production` is gated on, which is the call the Record button at the bottom of that screen actually makes. The quick-stock mode is not consulted.

**The reason the old gate carried is quoted rather than deleted**, because it was a real argument and it is worth knowing why it fails: *an absolute recounter has no business being handed a delta to apply.* This screen hands over no delta. It posts a production batch, and `routes/retail-production.js` writes the batch and moves the shelf inside one transaction, with no mode gate of its own — only a store-scope check on the restricted roles. **The proof was already shipped one row up the More list**: `logbatch` opens this same screen, with this same write, for a recount-mode operator, and always has. A gate that refuses from one door what it grants from the other is not a rule; it is a defect with a comment on it.

### The second defect, fixed in the same change

`hdOpen` answered `true` unconditionally, while `push()` silently declines a route the operator cannot reach. An operator holding `restock:fulfil` without `production:log` therefore closed the request and got nothing: no screen, and `kqAdvance`'s early return skipping even the re-render. `hdOpen` now asks `canRoute('whatmade')` first and returns false, so the caller falls through to the queue exactly as it does for a request with nothing to hand over.

### The suite proved a state the app cannot be in

`scripts/test_mobile_production.js` set `mode:'add'` in its fixture by hand, and the note beside it called that line load-bearing for the same reason `hdStart` did. Seventy assertions passed across every version of this flow while the flow itself was dead, because the fixture reproduced the only session that would have worked and no session can be it. **The fixture now says `mode:'recount'`**, which is what every operator who can reach these screens actually holds, and the old code fails it. This is the general lesson and it is not new here: a fixture that asserts the state a gate wants, rather than the state the app is in, tests the gate against itself.

### Scope, and what is deliberately not changed

- **`public/stock.html` carries the identical gate and is not touched.** In that app the `kitchen` role does read `'add'`, so the flow works there; §48 retires the app.

  > **AMENDED 2026-09-07 (v4.145) — THIS LINE WAS WRONG, and the same symptom was reported a second time because of it.** It is true of the `kitchen` role and of no other. Every other operator who can open that app's *Production* queue — the owner, an admin, a `retail` operator, none of them `stock_app_only` — reads `'recount'` there exactly as they do in Tacet Mobile, so the handover was shut for them too. The roles confined to `/stock` are precisely the ones that did not need the fix; the reasoning covered the users who were not reporting it. **The word *Production* appears only in `/stock`** — Tacet Mobile calls the same screen *Kitchen queue* — which is how the second report named the app the first fix had skipped.
  >
  > **`/stock` now takes the same gate**, and because that app holds no capability list of its own the answer is computed server-side: `mayLogProduction(req)` in `lib/quick-stock-grant.js`, beside the `quickStockMode` it replaces, shipped as `can_log_production` on `/api/retail-admin/quick-stock/context`. One derivation, both apps. It carries **no `req.backendUser` requirement** — unlike `mayRecount` beside it, this is not a revocable grant but the capability the write already enforces, and the legacy kitchen realm can genuinely post to that endpoint — and it **fails open** on an unresolvable capability set, as Tacet Mobile's `mCan()` does.
  >
  > **The Log a batch tile on `/stock` stays on the mode.** That tile carries its own decision, written where it stands: stating what a batch yielded is the kitchen's job, and a warehouse recount has no batches. The handover is not that case — the operator reaching it has just closed a kitchen request. §59's Tacet Mobile argument leaned on `logbatch` already opening the same screen for a recount-mode operator; that premise does not hold here, and the ruling does not need it.
  >
  > **A second suite was asserting the defect.** `scripts/test_stock_home.js` held `a-recount-operator-gets-the-queue-back`, defending it as *a warehouse recount has no business being sent to a screen that adds*. Two honest cases replace it. Where the section below says a fixture must not assert the state a gate wants, add this: **a green suite is not evidence the flow works when the suite's own case was written to match the gate.**

  > **AMENDED AGAIN 2026-09-07 (v4.147) — THE GATE WAS NOT THE WHOLE CAUSE.** Both amendments above were real and neither closed the report, because `hdStart` carried two further refusals that were silence rather than an answer. **`state.qs.items` starts `null`** and is filled two CHAINED round trips after the queue first renders — `loadQsCtx`, then `loadQsItems` on its answer — and `hdResolve` matches by SKU against that list. A list that has not arrived marks **every** line unmatched, and `!lines.some(l => l.id != null)` then refused to open at all. An operator tapping through faster than two round trips on a phone, or whose shelf fetch failed, closed the request and got nothing. Reproduced, not reasoned: set `items` to `null` — its real initial value — and the tap produces the reported silence exactly.
  >
  > **A late shelf is not a missing product.** The lines are held and the screen opens now, in its loading state; `loadQsItems` resolves them when the shelf lands. A shelf that never lands gets a named failure carrying the way forward — Retry, and the batch door that needs no request — because the request is already closed by the time anybody is on that screen and there is no way back to it.
  >
  > **Not one line matched is a sentence, not a silence.** The screen has always drawn an unmatched line greyed, badged *Not on this store's list*, with the count named underneath. Refusing to open threw that away and left nothing in its place — strictly worse than the problem it avoided, since a request whose lines this store cannot take is exactly what somebody needs to be told.
  >
  > **What still refuses**, all three about the request or the operator rather than the app's own readiness: no `production:log`; a request with nothing asked for; and no store to add to *once the context has answered and said so*, since `hdCommit` sends `store_id`.
  >
  > **Both apps, in the same commit.** `public/stock.html` carries the identical pair and is fixed alongside rather than reasoned about. Its shelf loads at boot, so the race is *less* likely there — recorded as a fact, never again as a reason to leave a file out.
  >
  > **The third fixture lesson, and the sharpest.** §59 said a fixture must not assert the state a gate wants; v4.145 added that a green suite is not evidence when its own case was written to match the gate; this adds that **a fixture whose stubs answer instantly cannot see a race the real network has.** Every suite set `items` by hand and every stub resolved in a microtask, so no case had ever run the ordinary path where the shelf is still in flight.

  > **AMENDED A THIRD TIME 2026-09-07 (v4.148) — THE SILENCE WAS THE REAL DEFECT, and removing it should have come first.** Each of the three amendments above removed a genuine cause; none of them removed the silence, which is why one bug took four rounds. `hdStart` returned a bare `false` on every refusal and `kqAdvance` fell back to the queue without a word, so an operator who had just closed a request saw an empty list and nothing else — whichever refusal had fired, and with no way to tell which.
  >
  > **Every refusal now names itself.** `hdStart` returns `true` when the screen opened and otherwise `nocap`, `nolines` or `nostore`, which `kqAdvance` turns into a sentence on the queue. It is a **note, not an error** — nothing failed, and the operator did the right thing; what is wrong is the state they are now in. It renders **above the empty state** as well as the list, because *Nothing to make* with no explanation is exactly the screen this defect showed somebody: a queue that has just gone quiet reads as success. `nocap` names `production:log` by the label an admin sees on the permissions screen, so the operator can ask for the right thing rather than report a blank screen.
  >
  > **The general rule, which is worth more than the three sentences: a refusal that lands on somebody who has just changed state — a request closed, the stock still short — may not be silent.** Silence there does not read as *nothing happened*. It reads as *that worked*.
  >
  > **And the fourth lesson in this section's run:** a diagnosis is impossible when the failure has no voice. The first three rounds were spent guessing between causes the app could have named.
- **Neither production screen names which store it is adding to.** `state.qs.storeId` is the first active store from the context response and there is no picker. This is pre-existing, shared with Log a batch, and unchanged by this ruling — recorded here so it is not re-derived, and left for its own change.
- No schema change, no migration, no capability grant changes, no new strings.

## §60 — A KITCHEN TYPES ITS BATCH ON THE CARD; A RECOUNT KEEPS THE SHEET

Decided by Ash, 2026-09-07, from the report that entering a batch still took two
taps: *"i want to click one time on the number and input a number directly. now
need 2 click."* Two mockups were put up and **Option B was chosen.**

### What was wrong

§46's add door had just been given a keypad (v4.142): tapping the count on an
Add stock card opened the shared ask sheet with a Quantity field. That removed
the hundred-and-thirty taps and left a smaller defect behind, which is what this
ruling is about.

**The sheet opened with nothing focused.** `sheetAsk()` renders its `<input>`
with no `autofocus` and no `focus()` call, so the keyboard stayed down until a
SECOND tap landed on the field. One tap to open the sheet, one to reach the
field it exists for. The field also asked for `inputmode="text"` — the full
keyboard rather than a number pad — for a control that accepts only digits.

### The ruling

**In add mode the count IS the field.** One tap turns the cell into an
`<input inputmode="numeric">` with the caret already in it; the commit button
takes the correction door's place on the card while it is open; there is no
sheet. **In recount mode the sheet stays**, and the two are reached by different
functions on purpose.

**The asymmetry is the ruling, not an inconsistency.** A recount is a bounded
decision about a figure that is not the operator's own, it is the number §46
guards, and the drop fork hangs off it — a sheet naming the product and offering
Cancel is the right shape for one of those. A kitchen entering what it made is
the opposite: its own count, no fork on the way up, and twenty of them in a row
down a list a sheet would cover between every one.

### What the change must not do, and how each is held

- **The two writes stay apart (§46).** `qsTypeOpen` and `qsAskCount` are
  separate functions, not one function branching on mode — deriving one from the
  other is how a delta and an absolute count become one write. While the count
  is being typed the correction door is **not on the card at all**: the commit
  button stands in its place, so the two are never one fat finger apart even for
  the moment the keyboard is up.
- **The shelf total still never seeds this control (§46).** The field opens on
  the pending amount, and empty at the usual +0 — a "0" would have to be cleared
  before anything could be typed over it.
- **Typing never re-renders.** This is the rule already written at the head of
  the Onwards commands and learned on the waste picker: `render()` rewrites the
  whole app in one `innerHTML`, and destroying a field under a thumb does not
  reliably keep an Android soft keyboard up — Ash saw it drop a letter at a
  time. `qsTyped` stores the digits and does nothing else; no `render()`, no
  `state.focus`. The one focus this control arms is the tap that opens it.
- **The digits are held in state, not read off the DOM at commit**, so they
  survive a render this card did not ask for — a toast, or a poller's dot
  changing state.
- **A non-number is not stripped to the digits inside it.** `13o` silently
  becoming `13` writes a quantity nobody entered, so the field stays open and
  says why. That message carries **no Retry**: Retry belongs to a failed write,
